976:
Commercial customer means any firm, person, entity corporation or organization that owns a commercial unit.
Commercial unit means any structure, whether freestanding or designed to serve multiple tenants, the primary purpose of which is conducting business.
Company means any organization, firm, person, entity, corporation or other business that contracts with the city to provide for the collection and disposal of solid waste material as defined in this article.
Customer or consumer is defined as any firm, person, entity, corporation or organization that owns property with any habitable structure in the city, whether it is for residential living or business, that is not exempt from or relieved of the duty to pay the city's regular monthly solid waste removal service charge by reason of his failure or refusal to accept the solid waste service when such service is available.
Hazardous waste means material in a solid or semi-solid state resulting from the manufacture or use of pesticides or drugs (other than normal household use), pathological wastes, chemical wastes, flammable or explosive material, and similar waste material in a solid or semi-solid state that the city may consider a likely hazard to the public health or safety, except radioactive waste materials, as provided in the rules of the state department of natural resources.
Industrial waste or industrial solid waste means the solid wasted materials from factories, processing plants and manufacturing enterprises, and includes food processing wastes, meat and poultry processing waste, hatchery waste, construction and demolition waste, condemned food, ashes and cinders from power plants, agriculture products waste, land clearance waste, and similar waste.
Residential unit means any structure, including single-family and multifamily dwellings, the primary purpose of which is living. Replacement of the 95-gallon cart shall be sixty dollars ($60.00) if lost or stolen.
Solid waste means residential and commercial non-recyclable waste, residential and commercial recyclable waste.
Waste means all perishable and nonperishable solid, semisolid and liquid wastes, including residential or commercial garbage, trash, refuse, paper, rubbish, ashes, manure, vegetable or animal solid and semisolid wastes, and other discarded solid and semisolid wastes.
Yard trimmings is defined as leaves, brush, grass, weeds, shrub and tree pruning no longer than five (5) feet in length or more than five (5) inches in diameter, Christmas trees, and vegetative residuals and matter resulting from landscaping development and maintenance other than mining, agricultural and silvicultural operations.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13; Ord. No. 141-020, 8-17-20)
977:
(a) All solid waste must be deposited in plastic bags securely tied with appropriate closure strips so that the contents thereof do not spill and place in covered plastic or metal garbage cans for disposal. It shall be unlawful to fail to store solid waste cans in the rear of the property or as close to the rear as possible on the side of the property to reduce their visibility from the public right-of-way.
(b) Yard trimmings shall not be placed in a plastic bag but, shall be placed in watertight paper bags or cardboard boxes which, when full, do not exceed fifty (50) pounds.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
978:
(a) Solid waste and yard trimmings shall be separated and placed on curbside in front of residence or business, or other place designated by the sanitation department of the city, no earlier than 5:00 p.m. of the day prior to the schedule pickup.
(b) Garbage cans and dumpsters shall be removed from the curbside no later than dawn on the day after the scheduled pickup. Garbage cans and dumpsters shall be stored in the rear of the property or as close to the rear as possible on the side of the property to reduce its visibility from the public right-of-way.
(c) Dumpsters at multifamily dwelling units and commercial dumpsters shall be enclosed and stored at the rear of the property so as to prevent visibility from the public right-of-way.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
979:
The manager of the solid waste division of the public works department shall see that all sweepings and solid waste within the limits of the city are removed to some suitable place to be approved by the manager, and the manager shall give similar directions about any and all things in the city which, in his discretion, should be removed for the protection of the health of the citizens of this city.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
980:
(a) The removal and safe disposal of all debris resulting from repairs, remodeling, construction or demolition are the responsibility of the owner of the property to engage the services of the City of East Point for such removal.
(b) It shall be unlawful to dispose of exposed used needles or lancets through use of the city's solid waste collection system. All such needles and lancets shall be disposed as provided by city code section 6-2015.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13; Ord. No. 141-020, 8-17-20)
981:
All grocery stores, markets, restaurants or other places of business handling or selling fruits, vegetables, groceries or other articles of food shall be classified as a large commercial customer and shall place all refuse of vegetables, fish and similar matter shall be kept in air tight securely fastened bags and placed in a commercial dumpster for disposal.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
982:
It shall be unlawful for any person to dump any garbage, trash, papers or solid waste on any city property.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
983:
(a) A monthly solid waste removal fee is hereby levied and assessed against all of property owners of the various classes, kinds and sizes of improved building lots of land and improvements thereon to be served or benefited by the city's removal of solid waste there from, however, that the maximum monthly solid waste removal fee per family dwelling unit on any improved building lot shall be as specified in section 7-2009; provided, further, that a building lot shall consist of any lot of land with a building thereon, and no building lot shall be considered "improved" unless there is a building thereon.
(b) All charges payable by a person, firm or corporation under the provisions of this division, which shall be and remain unpaid for a period of thirty (30) days after the same becomes due and payable, shall be subject to the imposition of a lien upon the lot or other tract of land owned by such person, firm or corporation and to which such service is delivered or made available, and shall be enforced in the same manner as are delinquent taxes by the issuance of execution. In addition to the enforcement remedy of issuing executions, the customer care department is hereby authorized to issue an order and to have the water connection which feeds the line to such tract of land disconnected as in the case of delinquent water use.
(c) In addition to the charges imposed for garbage and refuse collection by the city for commercial customers as set forth in this section, the city shall be authorized to add a fifteen (15) percent administrative fee to cover its costs for all billing and collections procedures, and related activities.
(d) Each new customer shall be required to submit a security deposit with the city as a condition of service. The amount of the security deposit and associated terms and conditions shall be pursuant to policies and procedures established by the city manager or their designee.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13; Ord. No. 141-020, 8-17-20)
984:
(a) The fee charged for the removal of solid waste from residences is hereby fixed at twenty-one dollars and fifty cents ($21.50) per month for one 95-gallon cart with an additional charge of six dollars ($6.00) per each additional cart. Single family residences include both owner-occupied and rented detached homes. Duplexes and quadraplex small rental apartment building units shall receive the same services as single family residences and are considered to be their equivalent under this section.
(b) Multifamily residences with a central dumpster collection will be charged eighteen dollars ($18.00) per month per dwelling unit unless a waiver has been granted prior to the adoption of this provision. Multifamily residences are defined herein to be each of the individual dwelling units in an apartment complex which provides for central dumpster collection of household solid waste.

(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13; Ord. No. 141-020, 8-17-20)
985:
(a) At the request of a resident the solid waste division will schedule a special pickup appointment for the collection of bulk materials such as discarded appliances ("white goods") or large items of furniture. The required charges for this service are in addition to the standard monthly sanitation charge. The minimum amount of tax or fee for this pick-up is thirty-five dollars ($35.00) per collection for one item, with a ten dollar ($10.00) charge for each additional item to be picked up during the same appointment. (See attached chart).
(b) Where the bulk materials to be disposed of are non-standard, the manager of the solid waste division of the public works department or his/her designee will make an inspection trip to the requesting resident's premises to provide an estimated charge prior to removal.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
986:
(a) Effective _______ from the effective date of this ordinance all commercial customers shall thereafter be required to engage the services of the City of East Point for the provision of commercial solid waste collection and disposal services within the city.
(b) The city shall grant to one company, an exclusive basic service agreement to use the public streets, alleys, roads and thoroughfares within the city for the purpose of operating and engaging in the business of collecting and disposing of commercial solid waste; and providing service pursuant to the contract, placing and servicing containers, operating trucks, vehicles and trailers, and such other operations and activity as are customary and/or incidental to the business of commercial solid waste collection and disposal. It shall be illegal for any company to operate outside the terms of this ordinance.
(c) All commercial establishment within the corporate limits of the city must subscribe to this service, through the city's customer care department. Mandatory subscription ensures that commercial solid waste is properly collected and disposed of in a manner that protects the health and safety of city residents. Likewise, the company shall collect and deliver for disposal all commercial solid waste accumulated within the corporate limits of the city by the city's commercial customers. The company will furnish the personnel and equipment to provide the services described herein and as contracted with the city, in an efficient and businesslike manner.
(d) The company that operates in the city providing solid waste collection and disposal services shall meet the following minimum requirements.
(1) Obtain a solid waste handling permit from the director of the environmental protection division of the state department of natural resources, pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 12-8-24.
(2) Use only vehicles and containers which comply with state EPD rules. Waste collection vehicles must be compactor-type trucks, covered or enclosed vehicles, constructed to be substantially leak proof, constructed of durable metal, easily cleanable and designed to prevent litter from escaping during transport. Recycling vehicles shall not be the same ones used for waste collection. Vehicles shall also meet all safety, size and weight requirements of the state department of transportation.
(e) Any person, firm or corporation under this provision found to be operating within the corporate limits of the city without an exclusive contract for services with the city shall be assessed a penalty violation fee in an amount no greater than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) for each container placed or serviced.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13; Ord. No. 141-020, 8-17-20)
987:
(a) The solid waste removal service charge shall be due and payable by each person liable therefore at the same time that water and electric bills are due and payable.
(b) Each person liable for such monthly solid waste service charge shall be billed for same by the treasurer at the same time that water and electric bills are rendered each month.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
988:
(a) No person shall be exempt from or relieved of the duty to pay the city's regular monthly solid waste removal service fee by reason of his failure or refusal to accept the solid waste service when such service is available.
(b) Commercial customers, however, may request and receive relief of this charge if the following conditions are met:
(1) The water service has been disconnected, or the water services is still active, but no more than one thousand (1,000) gallons of water have been consumed within the billing cycle; and
(2) The electric service has been disconnected and is no longer in service; and
(3) The commercial garbage container has been removed from the premises or request for container removal has been made to the customer care department.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13; Ord. No. 141-020, 8-17-20)
989:
It shall be unlawful for any person liable to the city for any solid waste removal service charge to fail or refuse to pay the same when due.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
990:
All bills for solid waste or sanitary charges are due and payable upon receipt. Failure of the consumer to pay all amounts owing by the fifteenth of the month following billing shall subject the consumer to discontinuance of service. All bills not paid in full by the fifteenth of the month following billing shall be subject to a service charge of ten (10) percent of the amount of such bill plus the current charges in accordance with section 7-2013.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
991:
The solid waste division shall not be required to collect solid waste from individual garbage containers at apartment houses, including public housing projects, containing four (4) or more living units, except in such instances where there is no access for mechanized equipment.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
992:
The owners of apartment complexes, including the public housing authority, which consist of four (4) or more living units, shall furnish commercial dumpsters in sufficient number to adequately contain the solid waste disposal at such location. The type, size, number and location of such commercial dumpsters required shall be subject to the approval of the manager of the solid waste division of the public works department. Notwithstanding any of the foregoing provisions, the manager of solid waste division may impose such policies or rules and regulations as he may deem appropriate from time to time for the more efficient operation of collection of solid waste.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
993:
Plans and specifications for the construction of apartment houses, or other multiple unit dwellings, containing more than four (4) units, shall be submitted to the department of planning and zoning, and shall show the location for commercial dumpsters, and pickup points. Such locations shall be in conformity with section 7-2003 of this chapter, and shall, with the exception of commercial dumpsters, be located at a point not more than one hundred (100) feet from the nearest point accessible to the trucks. The commercial dumpsters shall be located as required by the manager of the solid waste division of the department of public works whose approval shall be a condition precedent to the granting of a building permit by the building inspector. Any new pavement proposed by the developer/engineer shall be heavy duty pavement, of a depth to withstand the weight of the loaded garbage trucks servicing such sites, and as specified by the design engineer.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
994:
In the event that any person otherwise subject to the solid waste removal tax imposed by section 7-2008 is exempt from taxation by virtue of any ordinance, state statute or regulation, or federal law or regulation, then that person or entity shall either provide for itself solid waste removal at least twice weekly from all premises owned by that person or entity within the city by a person or firm approved in advance by the manager of the solid waste division of the department of public works or shall utilize the solid waste removal services of the solid waste division and shall pay for said services a monthly solid waste removal charge to the city in an amount equal to the solid waste removal tax otherwise imposed by this chapter.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
995:
It shall be unlawful for any owner or occupant of property within a residential district of the city to place any discarded appliances, items of furniture or other bulk items upon the premises or upon the right-of-way except that:
(1) Any owner or occupant desiring to discard bulk materials shall contact the sanitation department to schedule an appointment for the pickup of said materials and is subject to fees as outlined below.
(2) The pick-up fee for bulk materials is fixed at thirty-five dollars ($35.00) for the first ten (10) cubic yards of bulk materials and ten dollars ($10.00) per cubic yard for each additional cubic yard of bulk materials. Said fees will be applied to the utility account of the customer, or in the event there is no identified customer, the property owner.
(3) If said bulk material remains in the right-of-way without appointment for removal by the solid waste division, the owner or occupant of the property will be given notice to remove the bulky material within forty-eight (48) hours by the city.
(4) Property owners who fail to schedule a pick-up, and leave bulk materials on their property or upon the right-of-way for forty-eight (48) hours or more are subject to being cited by the city and upon being found in violation by the municipal court judge, may be fined at the maximum penalty fee allowed for such an offense under the law. Such a fine shall be in addition to any applicable pick-up fees outlined above and shall be set at a minimum of seventy dollars ($70.00) and shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00).
(5) Property owners shall be responsible for the bulk items left behind by their tenants and shall pay any outstanding bulk-rate removal and penalty fees when the tenant fails to pay said charges.
a. When a tenant fails to do so, within forty-eight (48) hours, property owners must schedule a pickup of bulk items and other items left behind by the tenant.
b. When a tenant fails to do so, property owners must pay the outstanding bulk-rate removal and penalty fees.
c. When a tenant leaves bulk or other items behind and fails to schedule a pickup, the city shall, in writing, notify the owner and/or tenant and/or any user and/or responsible party in possession of the property on which the violation exists, to abate the violation within forty-eight (48) hours after receipt of notice.
d. Notice shall be by personal service or certified mail addressed to the owner and/or tenant and/or any user and/or responsible party in possession of the property. If such person(s) cannot be located, notice shall be affected by posting a notice on the subject property. If notice is sent by certified mail and the notice is not returned or return receipt is not received within ten (10) days of sending the notice, notice shall be posted on the subject property.
e. The notice shall order that the violation of this section be abated within forty-eight (48) hours of receipt thereof. The notice shall also set a hearing date for five (5) days after receipt of this notice to be held if the violation is not abated within forty-eight (48) hours of receipt of the notice.
f. Failure to abate the violation within forty-eight (48) hours shall cause the city to take all such appropriate measures to ensure compliance with this section, up to and including causing the violation, after hearing on such failure, to be removed at the outstanding bulk-rate removal and penalty fees.
g. A hearing on the failure to abate the violation shall be set for and held five (5) days after receipt of the notice to abate the violation.
h. The owner and/or any user and/or responsible party in possession of the property shall be liable for all bulk-rate removal fees, penalties, fines assessed by the city court and any storage costs associated with removal by city equipment and city employees.
i. Citation for violation of this section does not relieve the owner, tenant, any user or responsible party in possession of the property from liability for violations of any other section of the city code.
(6) A property owner's failure to pay outstanding bulk-rate fees will subject the resident at the property to the utilities being cut off or the denial of utility services to the next resident at the identified property address. No utilities services shall be extended until the outstanding bulk-rate fees are paid in full.
(7) It shall be the policy of the city to waive bulk pick-up service fees to organizations sponsoring community clean-up days in specified areas and upon four (4) weeks' notice to solid waste division of the planned event. Such community clean-up days shall not exceed two (2) per year.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
996:
(a) There is hereby created a program operated by the city for the collection of recyclable paper, aluminum, glass and other recyclable materials. All persons, firms or corporations may separate from normal solid waste said recyclable material.
(b) All of said recyclable materials shall be placed separately at the curb on days specified by the solid waste division for collection and pursuant to such other rules and regulations as may be prescribed. Recyclable aluminum, glass and other materials shall be placed for collection in recycling bins supplied by the city. Recyclable paper shall be placed for collection in recycling bins or kraft bags or tied securely with rope or cord in packages not exceeding fifty (50) pounds.
(c) The manager of the solid waste division may prescribe and publish reasonable rules and regulations to administer the purposes of this section.
(d) It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation other than the owner, lessee or occupant of the premises to pickup said recyclable materials.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
998:
All public authorities and agencies having supervision of properties of this city are authorized, empowered, and instructed to establish and maintain receptacles for the deposit of litter and solid waste at appropriate locations where the property is frequented by the public, to post signs directing persons to the receptacles and serving notice of the provisions of Code sections 7-2021 through 7-2026, and to otherwise publicize the availability of such receptacles and requirements of Code sections 7-2021 through 7-2026.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
999:
It shall be unlawful for any person to set fire to the contents of, indiscriminately scatter or disperse the contents of, or otherwise vandalize any containers provided by any county or city for the dumping of solid waste.
(Ord. No. 023-13, 8-19-13)
1003:
The purpose of this article is to protect the public health, safety, environment, and general welfare through the regulation and prevention of litter. The objectives of this ordinance are:
(1) Provide for uniform prohibition throughout the City of East Point of any and all littering on public or private property; and
(2) Prevent the desecration of the beauty and quality of life of the city and prevent harm to the public health, safety, environment, and general welfare, including the degradation of water and aquatic resources caused by litter.
(Ord. No. 007-07, § 1.1, 12-19-06)
1004:
This article shall apply to all public and private property within the City of East Point.
(Ord. No. 007-07, § 1.2, 12-19-06)
1005:
The requirements of this article should be considered minimum requirements, and where any provision of this article imposes restrictions different from those imposed by any other ordinance, rule or regulation, or other provision of law, whichever provisions are more restrictive or impose higher protective standards for human health or the environment shall be considered to take precedence.
(Ord. No. 007-07, § 1.3, 12-19-06)
1006:
If the provisions of any article, section, subsection, paragraph, subdivision or clause of this article shall be judged invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, such order of judgment shall not affect or invalidate the remainder of any article, section, subsection, paragraph, subdivision or clause of this article.
(Ord. No. 007-07, § 1.4, 12-19-06)
1007:
Litter means any organic or inorganic waste material, rubbish, refuse, garbage, trash, hulls, peelings, debris, grass, weeds, ashes, sand, gravel, slag, brickbats, metal, plastic, and glass containers, broken glass, dead animals, discarded construction materials, abandoned construction materials, or intentionally or unintentionally discarded materials of every kind and description which are not "waste" as such term is defined in O.C.G.A., § 16-7-51, paragraph 6.
Person means any individual, including both landlords and tenants, partnership, firm, association, joint venture, public or private corporation, trust, estate, commission, board, public or private institution, utility, cooperative, city, county or other political subdivision of the State, any interstate body or any other legal entity.
Public or private property means the right of way of any road or highway; any body of water or watercourse or the shores or beaches thereof any park, playground, building, refuge, or conservation or recreation area; timberlands or forests; and residential, commercial, industrial, or farm properties.
(Ord. No. 007-07, § 2, 12-19-06)
1011:
No person shall operate any motor vehicle with a load on or in such vehicle unless the load on or in such vehicle is adequately secured to prevent the dropping or shifting of materials from such load onto the roadway.
(Ord. No. 007-07, § 4, 12-19-06)
1012:
It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision or fail to comply with any of the requirements of this article. Any person who has violated or continues to violate the provisions of this article may be subject to the enforcement actions outlined in this division or may be restrained by injunction or otherwise sentenced in a manner provided by law. Where the violation occurs on rental property, either the landlord or tenant (or both) may be held responsible for such violation.
(Ord. No. 007-07, § 5.1, 12-19-06)
1013:
(a) Whenever litter is thrown, deposited, dropped or dumped from any motor vehicle, boat, airplane, or other conveyance in violation of this article, it shall be prima facie evidence that the operator of the conveyance has violated this article. However, the lawful distribution of newsletters, political publications, religious publications and other written communications shall not constitute litter.
(b) Except as provided in subsection (a), whenever any litter which is dumped, deposited, thrown or left on public or private property in violation of this article is discovered to contain any article or articles not easily obtainable in the public domain, including but not limited to letters, bills, publications or other writing which display the name of the person thereon in such a manner as to indicate that the article belongs or belonged to such person, it shall be a rebuttable presumption that such person has violated this article.
(Ord. No. 007-07, § 5.2, 12-19-06)
1014:
Any person who violates this article shall be guilty of a violation and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished as follows:
(1) By a fine of not less than two hundred dollars ($200.00) and not more than one thousand two hundred dollars ($1,200.00); and
(2) In addition to the fine set out in subsection (a) above, the violator shall reimburse the city for the reasonable cost of removing the litter when the litter is or is ordered removed by the city; and
(3) a. In the sound discretion of the municipal court, the person may be directed to pick up and remove from any public street or highway or public right-of way for a distance not to exceed one mile any litter he has deposited and any and all litter deposited thereon by anyone else prior to the date of execution of sentence; or
b. In the sound discretion of the municipal court, the person may be directed to pick up and remove any and all litter from any public property, private right-of-way, or with prior permission of the legal owner or tenant in lawful possession of such property, any private property upon which it can be established by competent evidence that he has deposited litter. Pick up and removal shall include any and all litter deposited thereon by anyone prior to the date of execution of sentence; and
(4) The court may publish the names of persons convicted of violating this article.
(Ord. No. 007-07, § 5.3, 12-19-06)
1015:
All law enforcement agencies, officers and officials of this state and the City of East Point are hereby authorized, empowered and directed to enforce compliance with this article.
(Ord. No. 007-07, § 5.4, 12-19-06)
1018:
It shall be unlawful to overload, cruelly treat, maim, bruise, abuse, mistreat, torture, deprive of necessary sustenance, ill use, abandon, or otherwise wrongfully deal with any domestic animal or fowl or otherwise treat such domestic creatures in a harsh, inhumane or unreasonable manner. Shelter for horses, cattle or other domestic animals shall be provided to protect such creatures against inclement weather and extreme temperatures.
(Code 1959, § 5-2; Ord. No. 014-05, § 1, 8-1-05)
1019:
(a) The entire area embraced within the corporate limits of the city is hereby designated a bird sanctuary.
(b) It shall be unlawful to trap, hunt, shoot or attempt to shoot or molest in any manner any bird or wild fowl or to rob bird nests or wild fowl nests; provided, however, if starlings or similar birds are found to be congregating in such numbers in a particular locality that they constitute a nuisance or a menace to health or property in the opinion of the proper health authorities of the city, the health authorities shall meet with representatives of the Audubon Society, Bird Club, Garden Club or Humane Society, or as many of such clubs as are to be found to exist in the city, after having given at least three (3) days' actual notice of the time and place of such meeting to the representatives of such clubs.
(c) If as a result of such meeting no satisfactory alternative is found to abate such nuisance, such birds may be destroyed in such numbers and in such manner as is deemed advisable by the health authorities, under the supervision of the chief of police.
(Code 1959, § 5-1)
1020:
When the sanitation inspector shall be informed of any dead animal within the city, he shall cause all carcasses to be removed beyond the city limits and disposed of in such manner as not to create a nuisance.
(Ord. No. 925-86, § 1, 9-2-86)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 924-86, § 1, adopted Sept. 2, 1986, repealed § 7-3003, relative to the disposition of dead animals as derived from Code 1959, § 5-3. Ord. No. 925-86, § 1, enacted Sept. 2, 1986, adopted a new § 7-3003 to read as herein set out.
1021:
It shall be unlawful for any person to store or cause to be stored either on the premises of such person or other place within the city, the bodies of dead animals, fish or carnage of any kind, emitting an offensive odor.
(Code 1959, § 5-4)
1022:
No police officer shall kill or maim any domestic animal upon the streets or within the city, unless the destruction of such animal is necessary to prevent immediate and impending injury to a person or property.
(Code 1959, § 5-19)
1023:
It shall be unlawful for any person to put out or cause to be put out any poison within the city for the killing of any domestic animal.
(Code 1959, § 5-23)
State Law reference— Cruelty to animals, Ga. Code, §§ 26-7902—26-7904.
1024: Editor's note— Ord. No. 922-86, § 1, adopted Sept. 2, 1986, repealed §§ 7-3007 and 7-3008, which pertained to reporting lost animals to the police department and the return of an animal to its owner respectively. Former §§ 7-3007 and 7-3008 derived from Code 1959, §§ 5-20 and 5-21.
1025:
It shall be unlawful to turn out or allow any hogs, horses, cows, or similar animals to run at large within the city. Such stock allowed to do so shall be impounded, if possible, until the fine is paid if the guilty party be convicted of such offense.
(Code 1959, § 5-24)
Cross reference— Dogs running at large, § 7-3055.
1026:

The following definitions shall apply in the interpretation and enforcement of this article.
(1) Abandon. The word "abandon" shall mean the intentional act of leaving an animal to survive on its own or placing an animal upon public or private property or within a public building unattended or uncared for.
(2) Certificate. The word "certificate" shall mean a certificate issued at the time of vaccination of the dog, and bearing thereon the signature of the vaccinator, the vaccination tag number, the name, color, breed and sex of the dog, the name and address of the owner, and the date of expiration of the vaccination.
(3) Current license tag. The term "current license tag" shall mean a license tag issued for the year in question, except that a person shall have through April 30 of any year to secure a license tag for such a year provided a license tag for the prior year has already been purchased, and is affixed to the collar of the dog.
(4) Current vaccination tag. The term "current vaccination tag" shall mean a metal tag or certificate issued by the Georgia Department of Human Resources which bears a number showing that it is current for a one-year or a three-year period.
(5) Dog. The word "dog" shall mean dog, or any domesticated canine of either sex, whether or not vaccinated against rabies.
(6) Health officer. The words "health officer" shall mean the Commissioner of Health of Fulton County, or his authorized representative, which includes officers or employees of the Atlanta Humane Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals, Inc., so long as such corporation is under contract with Fulton County and City of East Point to operate the dog pound and perform animal and rabies control services.
(7) License tag. The term "license tag" shall mean a metal tag issued on behalf of East Point by the health officer and bearing the words "Fulton County" and a license number.
(8) Person. The word "person" shall be defined as in section 1-1003 of this Code.
(9) Pound. The word "pound" shall mean the facilities operated by the health officer for confining dogs impounded under the provisions of this regulation.
(10) Vaccinate. The word "vaccinate" shall mean the injection, by a veterinarian, of a specified dose of anti-rabies vaccine into the musculature of a dog, such vaccine having the U.S. Government license number approval stamped on label of vaccine container and having been approved by the State Department of Human Resources. Vaccine used for vaccination of dogs against rabies shall be refrigerated and kept under proper conditions, and shall show no signs of spoilage or otherwise be unfit for procuring immunity against rabies.
(11) Vaccination tag. The term "vaccination tag" shall mean a metal tag issued by the Georgia Department of Human Resources to licensed veterinarians in the State of Georgia and supplied by such veterinarians to owners upon vaccination.
(12) Veterinarian. The word "veterinarian" shall mean any person who holds a license to practice the profession of veterinary medicine issued by the state board of veterinary medicine.

As used in this chapter, the term:
(1) Adverse impact includes, but is not limited to, the following: any search warrants served on the property where controlled substances and/or weapons were seized; investigative purchases of controlled substances on or near the property by law enforcement agencies or their agents; arrests for violations of controlled substance law and or possession of weapons; loitering for the purposes of engaging in illegal activity; an increase in the volume of traffic associated with property; complaints made to law enforcement officials of illegal activity associated with the property; and finding of illegal weapons or controlled substances on or near property by law enforcement officials and their agents.
(2) Buildings, dwellings or structures mean any building or structure or part thereof used and occupied for human habitation, commercial, industrial, or business uses, or intended to be so used, and includes any outhouses and appurtenances belonging thereto or usually enjoyed therewith and also includes any building or structure of any design.
(3) Business means an activity, occupation, employment or enterprise, which requires time, attention, labor and material and wherein merchandise is exhibited or sold, or services offered.
(4) Closing means securing and causing a dwelling, building, or structure to be vacated.
(5) Director means the East Point Chief of Police or his duly authorized appointee.
(6) Disturbance means actions, behavior, or conduct by person or persons at a particular location that disturbs the peace.
(7) Drug crime means an act, which is a violation of Article 2 of Chapter 13 of Title 16 of the Official Code of Georgia Controlled Substances Act.
(8) Dwellings, buildings, or structures means any building or structure or part thereof used and occupied for human habitation, commercial, industrial, or business uses, or intended to be so used, and includes any outhouses and appurtenances belonging thereto or usually enjoyed therewith and also includes any building or structure of any design. As used in this chapter, the term "dwellings, buildings, or structures" shall not mean or include any farm, any building or structure located on a farm, or any agricultural facility or other building or structure used or the production, growing, raising, harvesting, storage, or processing of crops, livestock, poultry, or other farm products.
(9) Lot means a parcel of land with or without buildings, dwellings or structures.
(10) Nuisance means for purposes of this chapter, the condition existing whenever through violations of any of the following provisions resulting from separate incidents at a building, dwelling or structure, or immediately adjacent to the building, dwelling or structure or on any lot as a result of the operation of the business, twelve (12) or more points are accumulated within a period of six (6) months, or eighteen (18) or more points within a period of twelve (12) months, in accordance with the following point system. Where more than one (1) violation occurs during a single incident, the total points for the incident shall be the highest point value assigned to any single violation. The determination of the accumulation of points shall be made by the director.
(a) The following violations shall be assigned a point value of six (6) points:
(i) Controlled substances offenses;
(ii) Gambling offenses;
(iii) Prostitution offenses;
(iv) Illegal possession of firearms and other dangerous weapons;
(v) Offenses against children;
(vi) Offenses involving alcoholic beverages;
(vii) Possession of stolen property.
(viii) Permitting the premises to become disorderly, including suffering or permitting fighting or lewdness;
(ix) Disorderly conduct by individual or individuals; and
(x) Penal law violations, including but not limited to murder, attempted murder, assault, attempted assault, sex offenses etc.
(b) The following violations shall be assigned a point value of four (4) points:
(i) Violation of the fire prevention code (City Code section 6-2001 et seq);
(ii) Violation of any noise ordinance of the city;
(iii) Violation of the building code (City Code section 10-4001 et seq and 10-9001 et seq);
(iv) Violation of the property maintenance code (City Code section 7-7001 et seq);
(v) Violation of the zoning regulations of the city (City Code section 10-2001 et seq);
(vi) Any violation of Part 13 of the Code of Ordinances, City of East Point, Georgia, not addressed in subsections 7-4002(7)(a) or 7-4002(7)(c); and
(vii) Allowing persons on the premises in excess in excess of occupancy limits.
(c) The following violations shall be assigned a point value of three (3) points:
(i) Any violation of Part 7 of the Code of Ordinances, City of East Point, Georgia, not addressed in subsections 7-4002(7)(a) or 7-4002(7)(b);
(ii) Operating a business at the premises in a manner which causes it to be a source of disruption for the neighborhood and/or a focal point of police attention; and
(iii) General disturbances at a particular location.
(11) Occupant means any person (including domestic service employees) living and or sleeping in a dwelling unit or having possession of a space within a building, dwelling or structure.
(12) Operator means any person who has charge, care or control of a building, dwelling or structure, which is let or offered for occupancy.
(13) Owner means any person, agent, operator, firm, or corporation having a legal or equitable interest in the property; or recorded in the official records of the state, county or municipality as holding title to the property; or otherwise having control of the property, including the guardian of the estate or any such person, and the executor or administrator of the estate of such person if ordered to take possession of real property by a court.

(18) Repair means closing a dwelling, building, or structure or the cleaning or removal of debris, trash, or other materials present and accumulated which create a health or safety hazard in or about any dwelling, building, or structure.

1050:
(1) In any action under this Chapter, evidence of the common fame and general reputation of the building, dwelling or structure, of the inhabitants or occupants thereof, or of those resorting thereto, shall be competent evidence to prove the existence of a property or building nuisance.

(4) Any building, dwelling or structure or lot, wherein within a one year period prior to the commencement of an action under this chapter, there has been presented a preponderance of evidence of repeated criminal activity which has an adverse impact on such property or neighborhood, shall be prima facie evidence that a public nuisance exists at said location.

1051:
(1) The city attorney, upon request of the director or the city council, may bring and maintain a civil proceeding in the name of the city for the following types of relief: (a) permanent injunction, (b) temporary closing order, (c) temporary restraining order, or (d) temporary injunction.
(a) The city attorney shall name as defendants, the building, dwelling or structure or lot wherein the public nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted, by describing it by tax map number and/or street address and at least one of the owners of some part of or interest in the property.
(b) The city attorney shall bring and maintain a civil proceeding in the name of the city in the City Court of the City of East Point, or any other court of competent jurisdiction, including the Superior Court of Fulton County, to permanently enjoin the public nuisance and the persons, conducting, maintaining or permitting the public nuisance from further conducting, maintaining, or permitting the public nuisance. The owner, operator, and/or lessee of a building, dwelling, structure or lot wherein the public nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted may be made defendants in the action.
(c) The venue of such action shall be in the county where the public nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted.
(d) The existence of an adequate remedy at law shall not prevent the granting of temporary or permanent relief pursuant to this chapter.
(e) The civil action shall be commenced by the filing of a summons and complaint alleging the facts constituting the nuisance.
(f) The complaint shall name as defendants the building, dwelling, structure or lot wherein the nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted, by describing it by district and lot number and/or street address and at least one of the owners who possess some part of or an interest in the property.
(g) Any complaint filed under this chapter shall be verified or accompanied by affidavit(s) for purposes of showing that the owner or his/her agent has notice of the nuisance and has had an opportunity to abate the nuisance.
(h) The complaint or affidavit shall contain a description of the attempts by the applicant to notify and locate the owner of the property and/or the owner's agent.
(i) The complaint or affidavit shall describe the adverse impact associated with the property on the surrounding neighborhood.
(j) In rem jurisdiction shall be complete over the building, dwelling, structure or lot wherein the public nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted by affixing the summons to the door of the building, dwelling, structure or lot and by mailing the summons by certified or registered mail, return receipt requested, to one of the owners who possesses some part of or an interest in the property. Proof of service shall be filed within two (2) days thereafter with the clerk of the court designated in the summons. Service shall be complete upon such filing.
(k) Defendant(s), other than the building, dwelling, structure or lot wherein the public nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted, shall be served with the summons in any manner lawfully provided in the laws of the State of Georgia governing legal summons.
(l) With respect to any action commenced or to be commenced pursuant to this chapter, the city attorney shall file a notice of lis pendens pursuant to the provisions of O.C.G.A. 44-14-610 et seq..
(m) The owner of the real estate affected by the action shall be presumed to be the person in whose name the real estate is recorded in the office of the Clerk of Fulton County.
(n) Whenever there is testimony that a person was the manager, operator, supervisor, or in any other way in charge of the premises at the time a public nuisance was being conducted, maintained or permitted, such evidence shall be presumptive that he or she was an agent or employee of the owner or lessee of the building, dwelling, structure or lot considered to be a nuisance.
(o) If, upon the trial of an action under this chapter, or upon a motion for summary judgment in an action under this chapter, a finding is made that the defendant has conducted, maintained or permitted a public nuisance defined in this chapter, a penalty may be awarded in an amount not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) for each day it is found that the defendant conducted, maintained or permitted the public nuisance after notice to abate has been given by the city. Upon recovery, such penalty shall be paid into the general fund of the city.
(p) A judgment pursuant to this chapter shall be enforced by the city police department and the office of city attorney.
(3) Permanent injunction.
(a) A judgment awarding a permanent injunction, pursuant to this chapter, may direct the police department to seize and remove from the building, dwelling, structure or lot, all personal property, material, equipment and instrumentalities used in the creation and maintenance of the public nuisance and shall direct the sale by the police department of such property in the manner provided for the sale of personal property in the same manner as provided for the sale of unclaimed lost or stolen property in section 6-1028 of this Code. The net proceeds of any such sale, after deduction of the lawful expenses involved, shall be paid into the general fund of the city.
(b) A judgment awarding a permanent injunction pursuant to this chapter may authorize agents of the city to forthwith remove and correct construction and structural alterations in violation of city codes. Any and all costs associated with these repairs or alterations shall become a lien against said property and shall have priority before any mortgage or other lien that exists prior to such filing except tax and assessment liens and any nuisance abatement lien.
(c) A judgment awarding a permanent injunction, pursuant to this chapter, may direct the closing of the building, dwelling, structure or lot by the police department, to the extent necessary to abate the nuisance, and shall direct the police department to post a copy of the judgment and a printed notice of such closing. Mutilation or removal of such a posted judgment or notice while it remains in force, in addition to any other punishment prescribed by law, shall be punishable on conviction by a fine of not more than five hundred dolars ($500.00) or by imprisonment not exceeding fifteen (15) days, or by both, provided such judgment contains therein a notice of such penalty.
(d) The closing directed by the judgment shall be for such period as the court may direct, but in no event shall the closing be for a period of more than one (1) year from the posting of the judgment provided for in this subdivision.
(e) If the owner shall file a bond in the value of the property ordered to be closed and submits proof to the court that the nuisance has been abated and will not be created, maintained or permitted for such period of time as the building, dwelling, structure or lot has been directed to be closed in the judgment, the court may vacate the provisions of the judgment that direct the closing of the building, dwelling, structure or lot.
(f) A closing by the police department pursuant to this subdivision shall not constitute an act of possession, ownership or control by the police department of the closed premises.
(g) Intentional disobedience or resistance to any provision of a judgment awarding a permanent injunction pursuant to this chapter, in addition to any other punishment prescribed by law, shall be punishable by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), or by imprisonment not exceeding one hundred twenty (120) days, or by both.
(h) Upon the request of the city attorney, or the city council, the police department shall assist in the enforcement of a judgment awarding a permanent injunction entered in an action brought pursuant to this chapter.
(i) A judgment rendered awarding a permanent injunction pursuant to this chapter shall be and become a lien upon the building, dwelling, structure or lot named in the complaint in such action, such lien to date from the time of filing a notice of liens pending in the office of the clerk of the county wherein the building, dwelling, structure or lot is located. Every such nuisance abatement lien shall have priority before any mortgage or other lien that exists prior to such filing except tax and assessment liens.
(j) A judgment awarding a permanent injunction pursuant to this chapter shall provide, in addition to the costs and disbursements allowed by law, upon satisfactory proof by affidavit or such other evidence as may be submitted, the actual costs, expenses and disbursements of the city in investigating, bringing and maintaining the action.
(4) Preliminary injunction.
(a) Generally.
(i) Pending an action for a permanent injunction as provided for in this article, the court may grant a preliminary injunction enjoining a public nuisance within the scope of this chapter and the person or persons conducting, maintaining or permitting the public nuisance from further conducting, maintaining or permitting the public nuisance. An order granting the preliminary injunction shall direct a trial of the issues at the earliest possible time. Where preliminary injunction has been granted, the court shall render a decision with respect to a permanent injunction at its earliest convenience after the conclusion of the trial. A temporary closing order may be granted pending a hearing for a preliminary injunction where it appears by clear and convincing evidence that a nuisance within the scope of this chapter is being conducted, maintained or permitted and that the public health, safety or welfare immediately requires the granting of a temporary closing order. A temporary restraining order may be granted pending a hearing for a preliminary injunction where it appears by clear and convincing evidence that a nuisance within the scope of this chapter is being conducted, maintained or permitted.
(ii) A preliminary injunction shall be enforced by the city attorney and the police department.
(b) The city attorney shall show, by affidavit and such other evidence as may be submitted, that there is a cause of action for a permanent injunction abating a nuisance within the scope of this chapter.
(c) Temporary closing order.
(i) If, on a motion for a preliminary injunction, the city attorney shall show by clear and convincing evidence that a nuisance within the scope of this chapter is being conducted, maintained or permitted and that the public health, safety or welfare immediately requires a temporary closing order, a temporary order closing such part of the building, dwelling, structure or lot wherein the nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted may be granted without notice, pending order of the court granting or refusing the preliminary injunction and until further order of the court. Upon granting a temporary closing order, the court shall direct the holding of a hearing for the preliminary injunction at the earliest possible time; a decision on the motion for a preliminary injunction shall be rendered by the court at the earliest possible time.
(ii) Unless the court orders otherwise, a temporary closing order together with the papers upon which it was based and a notice of hearing for the preliminary injunction shall be personally served, in the same manner as a summons.
(d) Temporary restraining order.
(i) A temporary restraining order may be granted pending a hearing for preliminary injunction where it appears by clear and convincing evidence that a public nuisance within the scope of this chapter is being conducted, maintained, or permitted and that the public health, safety, or welfare immediately requires the granting of a temporary restraining order. This order shall restrain the defendants and all persons from removing or transferring off the property or in any manner interfering with the fixtures and movable property used in conducting, maintaining or permitting the public nuisance and from further conducting, maintaining or permitting the public nuisance. A temporary restraining order may be granted without notice, pending order of the court granting or refusing the preliminary injunction and until further order of the court. Upon granting a temporary restraining order, the court shall direct the holding of a hearing for the preliminary injunction.
(ii) Unless the court orders otherwise, a temporary restraining order and the papers upon which it was based and a notice of hearing for the preliminary injunction shall be personally served in the same manner as a summons.
(e) Temporary closing order; temporary restraining order.
(i) If on motion for a preliminary injunction, the city attorney submits evidence warranting both a temporary closing order and a temporary restraining order, the court shall grant both orders.
(ii) Temporary closing orders and temporary restraining orders shall be enforced by the city attorney and the police department.
(f) The officers serving a temporary restraining order, shall forthwith make and return to the court, an inventory of personal property situated in and used in conducting, maintaining or permitting a public nuisance within the scope of this chapter and shall enter upon the building, dwelling, structure or lot for such purpose. Such inventory shall be taken in any manner which is deemed likely to evidence a true and accurate representation of the personal property subject to such inventory including, but not limited to, photographing such personal property.
(g) The officers serving a temporary restraining order shall, upon service of the order, command all persons present in the building, dwelling, structure or lot to vacate the premises forthwith. Upon the building, dwelling, structure or lot being vacated, the premises shall be securely locked and all keys delivered to the officers serving the order who thereafter shall deliver the keys to the fee owner, lessor or lessee of the building, dwelling, structure or lot involved. If the fee owner, lessor or lessee is not at the building, dwelling, structure or lot when the order is being executed, the officers shall securely padlock the premises and retain the keys until the fee owner, lessor or lessee of the building is ascertained, at which time, the officers shall deliver the keys to such owner, lessor or lessee, if such individual resides within Fulton County.
(h) Upon service of a temporary restraining order, the officer shall post a copy thereof in a conspicuous place or upon one or more of the principal doors at entrances of such premises where the public nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted. In addition, where a temporary restraining order has been granted, the officers shall affix, in a conspicuous place or upon one or more of the principal doors at entrances of such premises, a printed notice that shall state that certain described activity is prohibited by court order and that removal of property is prohibited by court order. If the temporary restraining order directs that the premises are to be closed by court order, the notice shall contain the legend "Closed by Court Order" in block lettering of sufficient size to be observed by anyone intending or likely to enter the premises, the date of the order, the court from which issued and the name of the office or agency posting the notice. Mutilation or removal of such a posted order or such a posted notice while it remains in force, in addition to any other punishment prescribed by law, shall be punishable, on conviction, by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) or by imprisonment not exceeding one hudred twenty (120) days, or by both, provided such order or notice contains therein a notice of such penalty. The police department shall, upon the request of the office of city attorney, or upon the direction of the city council, assist in the enforcement of this subdivision.
(i) Intentional disobedience of, or resistance to, a temporary restraining order, in addition to any other punishment prescribed by law, shall be punishable, on conviction, by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) or by imprisonment not exceeding one hundred twenty (120) days or by both.
(j) A temporary restraining order or preliminary injunction shall not issue under this chapter, except upon the giving of a bond or security by the applicant, in the amount of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00), for the payment of such costs and damages as may be incurred or suffered by any party who is found to be wrongfully restrained or enjoined. A bond or security shall not be required of the State of Georgia, any municipal corporation of the State of Georgia or any political subdivisions of the State of Georgia.
(5) Temporary restraining order; defendant's remedies.
(a) Temporary restraining order to be vacated; inspection provision.
(i) A temporary restraining order shall be vacated, upon notice to the city attorney, if the defendant shows by affidavit and such other proof as may be submitted that the public nuisance within the scope of this chapter has been abated. An order vacating a temporary closing order, or a temporary restraining order shall include a provision authorizing agencies of the city to inspect the building, dwelling, structure or lot, which is the subject of an action pursuant to this chapter, periodically without notice, during the pendency of the action, for the purpose of ascertaining whether or not the public nuisance has been resumed. Intentional disobedience of, or resistance to, an inspection provision of an order vacating a temporary restraining order, in addition to any other punishment prescribed by law, shall be punishable, on conviction, by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) or by imprisonment not exceeding one hundred twenty (120) days, or by both. The police department shall, upon the request of the office of city attorney, or upon the direction of the city council, assist in the enforcement of an inspection provision of an order vacating a temporary restraining order.
(ii) A temporary restraining order may be vacated by the court, upon notice to the city attorney, when the defendant gives an undertaking and the court is satisfied that the public health, safety or welfare will be protected adequately during the pendency of the action. The undertaking shall be in an amount equal to the assessed valuation of the building, dwelling, structure or lot where the public nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted or in such other amount as may be fixed by the court. The defendant shall pay to the city, in the event a judgment of permanent injunction is obtained, its actual costs, expenses and disbursements in investigating, bringing and maintaining the action.
(b) When the defendant gives an undertaking in the amount of the civil penalty demanded in the complaint together with costs, disbursements and the projected annual costs of the prosecution of the action to be determined by the court, upon a motion on notice to the city attorney, a temporary injunction or a temporary restraining order shall be vacated by the court.
(6) Preliminary injunction of bulk transfer.
(a) Generally, pending an action pursuant to this chapter, the court may grant a preliminary injunction enjoining a defendant from making a bulk transfer, as defined in this section.
(b) If on a motion for a preliminary injunction of a bulk transfer, the city attorney shall show by clear and convincing evidence that a public nuisance within the scope of this chapter is being conducted, maintained, or permitted, a temporary restraining order may be granted, without notice, restraining the defendants and all persons from making or permitting a "bulk transfer," as defined in this article, pending order of the court granting or refusing the preliminary injunction and until further order of the court. Application for a temporary restraining order shall be made pursuant to subsection 7-4004(4).
(c) "Bulk transfer" defined. A "bulk transfer" is any transfer of a major part of the materials, supplies, merchandise or other inventory or equipment of the transferor in the building, dwelling, structure or lot where the public nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted that is not in the ordinary course of the transferor's business.
(d) A preliminary injunction shall be enforced by the office of city attorney or by the city police department.
(e) If the court grants a preliminary injunction, the provisions of the subsection 7-4004(4)(f) shall be applicable.
(7) Temporary receiver.
(a) In any action wherein the complaint alleges that the nuisance is being conducted or maintained in the residential portions of any building or structure or portion thereof, which are occupied in whole, or in part, as the home, residence or sleeping place of one (1) or more human beings, the court may, upon motion on notice by the plaintiff, appoint a temporary receiver to manage and operate the property during the pendency of the action, in lieu of a temporary closing order. A temporary receivership shall not continue after final judgment unless otherwise directed by the court. Upon the motion of any party, including the temporary receiver, or on its own initiative, the appointing court may remove a temporary receiver at any time.
(b) The temporary receiver shall have such powers and duties as the court shall direct, including, but not limited to collecting and holding all rents due from all tenants, leasing or renting portions of the building or structure, making or authorizing other persons to make necessary repairs or to maintain the property, hiring security or other personnel necessary for the safe and proper operation of a dwelling, prosecuting or defending suits flowing from his or her management of the property and retaining counsel therefore, and expending funds from the collected rents in furtherance of the foregoing powers.
(c) A temporary receiver, before entering upon his or her duties, shall be sworn or shall affirm faithfully and fairly to discharge the trust committed to such receiver. The oath or affirmation may be waived upon consent of all parties.
(d) A temporary receiver shall keep written accounts itemizing receipts and expenditures, and describing the property and naming the depository of receivership funds, which shall be open to inspection by any person having an apparent interest in the property. Upon motion of the temporary receiver, or of any person having an apparent interest in the property, the court may require the keeping of particular records, or direct or limit inspection, or require presentation of a temporary receiver's accounts. Notice of motion for the presentation of a temporary receiver's accounts shall be served upon the sureties on the temporary receiver's undertaking as well as upon each party.
(8) Chapter not exclusive remedy. This section 7-4004 shall not be construed to exclude any other remedy provided by law for the protection of the health, safety and welfare of the people of the City of East Point.
(Ord. No. 021-05, § 1, 9-6-05)
1052:
(1) In addition to and as an alternative to the enforcement procedures established elsewhere, the director, after giving notice and an opportunity for an administrative hearing may deem the existence of a public nuisance as such is defined thereunder and shall thereafter be authorized:
(a) To order the closing of the building, erection, place, or place of business to the extent necessary to abate the nuisance;
(b) To suspend for a period not to exceed six (6) months or revoke for a period of one (1) year a certificate of occupancy issued for such premises, and to prevent the operator from obtaining a new certificate of occupancy for another location for the period of suspension or revocation;
(c) To suspend for a period not to exceed six (6) months or revoke for a period of one (1) year any occupational license or permit issued by the city related to the conduct of a business or trade at the premises, which suspension or revocation shall also apply to any other locations operated by the holder for which the license or permit is required;
(d) To suspend for a period not to exceed six (6) months or revoke for a period of one (1) year eligibility to secure grants or loans from the city; or
(e) To order the demolition of such dwelling, building or structure; or
(f) Any combination of the above.
(2) Service of notice.
(a) Prior to the issuance of orders by the director pursuant to this section, the director shall give notice and opportunity for a hearing to the owner, lessor, lessee and mortgagee of a building, erection or place wherein the public nuisance is being conducted, maintained or permitted. Such notice shall be served upon an owner, lessor or lessee in same manner as a summons, and upon a mortgagee by means of certified mail, return receipt requested, sent to the mortgagee's last known address, provided that any service other than delivery to the person to be served shall be complete immediately upon delivery, mailing or posting without the necessity of filing proof of service with the clerk of any court before the hearing. The person in whose name the real estate affected by the orders of the director is recorded in the office of the county clerk shall be presumed to be the owner thereof. Proceedings shall be commenced by service of the notice and opportunity for a hearing within sixty (60) days after the occurrence of the most recent violation cited in the notice.
(b) The lack of knowledge of acquiescence or participation in or responsibility for a public nuisance on the part of the owners, lessors, lessees, mortgagees and all those persons in possession or having charge of as agent or otherwise, or having any interest in the property, real or personal used in conducting or maintaining the public nuisance, shall not be a defense by such owners, lessors and lessees, mortgagees and such other persons.
(3) Owners, lessors, lessees and mortgagees may appeal orders of the director immediately in the city court, and the filing of such appeal with the city court shall immediately stay an order until such time as the city court has heard and adjudicated the appeal.
(4) Orders of the director issued pursuant to this section shall be posted at the building, erection or place where a public nuisance exists or is occurring in violation of law and shall be mailed to the owner or record thereof within one (1) business day of the posting.
(5) Ten (10) business days after the posting of an order issued pursuant to this section and upon the written directive of the director, officers of the east point police department are authorized to act upon and enforce such orders, provided that no appeal has been filed pursuant to subsection 7-4005(3).
(6) Where the director closes a building, erection or place pursuant to this section, such closing shall be for such period as the director may direct, but in no event shall be closing be for a period of more than one (1) year from the posting of the order pursuant to this section. If the owner, lessor or lessee shall file a bond in an amount determined by the director but which may not exceed the value of the property ordered to be closed and submit proof satisfactory to the director that the nuisance has been abated and will not be created, maintained or permitted for such period of time as the building, erection or place has been directed to be closed by the order of the director, then the director may vacate the provisions of the order that direct the closing of the building, erection or place.
(7) It shall be a misdemeanor for any person to use or occupy or to permit any other person to use or occupy any building, erection or place, or portion thereof, ordered closed by the director. Mutilation or removal of a posted order of the director shall be punishable by a fine of not more than two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) or by imprisonment not exceeding fifteen (15) days, or both, provided such order contains therein a notice of such penalty.
(8) Intentional disobedience or resistance to any provision of the orders issued by the director pursuant to this section, in addition to any other punishment prescribed by law, shall be punishable by a fine or not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) or by imprisonment not to exceed one hundred twenty (120) days, or both.
(9) The director may promulgate rules and regulations to carry out and give full effect to the provisions of this section.
(10) If any provision of this section or the application thereof to any person or circumstances is held invalid, the remainder of this section and the applications of such provisions to other persons and circumstances shall not be rendered invalid thereby.
(Ord. No. 021-05, § 1, 9-6-05; Ord. No. 001-06, § 1, 3-20-06)
1053:
(1) Hardship waiver shall mean, for this section of this chapter, approval by the director to waive the compliance provisions of this chapter, as it applies to the accumulation of points under subsection 7-4002(7)(b) only. The hardship waiver shall not have the effect of waiving enforcement of the specific violations named in subsection 7-4002 (7)(b) or any other provision of the East Point Code of Ordinances. The hardship waiver acts only to waive the accumulation of points under this chapter to avoid director-approved property from being deemed a nuisance under this chapter.
(2) Any owner, occupant or responsible party who is subject to the provisions of subsection 7-4002(7)(b) of this chapter may apply for a hardship waiver. This section shall not apply to an owner or responsible party of rental property.
(3) A hardship waiver may be requested from the city when submitted in writing, to the director, within ten (10) calendar days of receipt of a notice of citation or a notice of a violation described in subsection 7-4002(7)(b). The owner, occupant or responsible party shall state the reasons why the strict enforcement of this chapter would result in an undue hardship.
(4) The director shall approve or deny such request within fifteen (15) days of submission of the hardship waiver request. The decision of the director shall be final.
(5) An approval of a request for a hardship waiver shall become effective as of the date of the citation or violation described in subsection 7-4002(7)(b). The waiver shall remain in effect for a period of twelve (12) months. During the twelve-month period, the owner, occupant or responsible party shall be responsible for all fines, fees and other penalties issued for violation of any of the code sections described in subsection 7-4002(7)(b). No points shall accrue for violation of any of the code sections described in subsection 7-4002(7)(b) while the hardship waiver is in effect for the specific property named.
(6) The hardship waiver may be renewed by the director, upon written request from the owner, occupant or responsible party. The director, may, at his or her discretion renew the hardship waiver for a period of twelve (12) months. The owner, occupant or responsible party continues to be responsible and liable for all fines, fees and other penalties upon violation of the code sections described in subsection 7-4002(7)(b).
(7) The hardship waiver granted pursuant to this section shall immediately terminate if the property is sold or if ownership otherwise changes.
(Ord. No. 021-05, § 1, 9-6-05)
1054:
If the owner or parties in interest fail to comply with an order to vacate and close or demolish the dwelling, building or structure the director of community services may cause such dwelling, building or structure to be repaired, altered or improved or to be vacated and closed or demolished; and the director of community services may cause to be posted on the main entrance of any building, dwelling or a structure so closed a placard with the following words:
"This building is unfit for human habitation or commercial, industrial, or business use; the use or occupancy of this building for human habitation or for commercial, industrial or business use is prohibited and unlawful."
(Ord. No. 001-06, § 1, 3-20-06)
1055:
If the owner fails to comply with any order to remove or demolish a dwelling, building or structure, the director may cause such dwelling, building or structure to be removed or demolished; provided, however, that the duties of the director, set forth in section 7-4007 and this section, shall not be exercised until the city council shall have by ordinance ordered the director to proceed to effectuate the purpose of this chapter with respect to the particular property or properties which the director shall have found to be unfit for human habitation or unfit for its current commercial, industrial, or business use, which property or properties shall be described in the ordinance.
(Ord. No. 001-06, § 1, 3-20-06)
1056:
(a) The amount of the cost of such vacating and closing or removal or demolition by the director shall be a lien against the real property upon which such cost was incurred. Said lien shall attach to the real property upon the payment of all costs of demolition by the city and the filing of an itemized statement of the total sum of said costs by the director in the office of the clerk of the city on a lien docket maintained by said clerk for such purposes. If the dwelling, building or structure is removed or demolished by the director he shall sell the materials of such dwellings, buildings, or structures and shall credit the proceeds of such sale against the cost of the removal or demolition and any balance remaining shall be deposited in the superior court by the director, shall be secured in such manner as may be directed by such court, and shall be disbursed by such court to the persons found to be entitled thereto by final order or decree of such court. Nothing in this chapter shall be power of the city to define and declare nuisances and to cause their removal or abatement by summary proceedings or otherwise.
(b) The city shall enforce the collection of any amount due on such lien for removal or demolition of dwellings buildings or structures in the following manner:
(1) The owner or parties at interest shall be allowed to satisfy the amount due on such lien by paying to the city within thirty (30) days after the perfection of said lien, a sum of money equal to twenty-five (25) percent of the total amount due and by further paying to the city the remaining balance due on such lien, together with interest at the rate of seven (7) percent per annum, in three (3) equal annual payments, each of which shall become due and payable on the anniversary date of the initial payment made as hereinabove prescribed;
(2) Should the property upon which such lien is perfected be sold, transferred, or conveyed by the owner or parties at interest at any time prior to the termination of the said three-year period, then the entire balance due on such lien shall be due and payable to the city; and
(3) Should the amount due on such lien, or any portion thereof, be unpaid after the passage of said three-year period, or upon the occurrence of the contingency provided for in subparagraph (2) of this paragraph, the city may enforce the collection of any amount due on such lien for alteration, repair, removal, or demolition of dwellings, buildings, or structures in the same manner as provided in Section 48-5-358 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated and the other applicable state statutes. This procedure shall be subject to the right of redemption by any person having any right, title to interest in or lien upon said property, all as provided by Article 3 of Chapter 4 of Title 48 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated.
