1057:
(a) Complaints or orders issued by the director pursuant to this chapter, shall, in all cases, be served upon each person in possession of said property, each owner, and each party in interest; and the return of service signed by the director or his agent or an affidavit of service executed by any citizen of this state, reciting that a copy of such complaint or orders was served upon each person in possession of said property, each owner, and each party in interest personally or by leaving such copy at the place of residence, shall be sufficient evidence as to the service of such person in possession, owner, and party interest.
(b) If any of the owners and parties in interest shall reside out of the city service shall be perfected by causing a copy of such complaint or orders to be served upon such part or parties by the sheriff or any lawful deputy of the county of the residence of such party or parties or such services may be made by any citizen; and the return of such sheriff or lawful deputy or the affidavit of such citizen, that such party or parties were served either personally or by leaving a copy of the complaint or orders at the residence, shall be conclusive as to such service.
(c) Nonresidents of this state shall be served by posting a copy of such complaint or orders in a conspicuous place on premises affected by the complaint or orders. Where the address of such nonresidents is known, a copy of such complaint or orders shall be mailed to them by registered or certified mail.
(d) In the event either the owner or any party in interest is a minor or an insane person or person laboring under disabilities, the guardian or other personal representative of such person, shall be served and if such guardian or personal representative resides outside the city or is a nonresident, he shall be served as provided for in subsection (c) of this section or this subsection in such cases. If such minor or insane person or person laboring under disabilities has no guardian or personal representative or in the event such minor or insane person lives outside the city or is a nonresident, service shall be perfected by serving such minor or insane person personally or serving such minor or insane person personally or by leaving a copy at the place of his residence which shall be sufficient evidence as to the service of such person or persons; in the case of other persons who live outside of the city or are nonresidents, service shall be perfected by serving the judge of the probate court of the county wherein such property is located who shall stand in the place of and protect the rights of such minor or insane person or appoint a guardian ad litem for such person.
(e) In the event the whereabouts of any owner or party in interest is unknown and the same cannot be ascertained by the director in the exercise of reasonable diligence and the director shall make an affidavit to that effect, then the service of such complaint or order upon such persons shall be made in the same manner as provided in subsection (c) of this section or service may be perfected upon any person, firm, or corporation holding itself out as an agent of the property involved.
(f) A copy of such complain or orders shall also be filed in the proper office or offices for the filing of lis pendens notice in the county in which the dwelling, building, or structure is located and such filing of the complaint or orders shall have the same force and effect as other lis pendens notices provided by law. Any such complaint or orders or an appropriate lis pendens notice may contain a statement to the effect that a lien may arise against the described property and that an itemized statement of such lien is maintained on a lien docket maintained by the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 001-06, § 1, 3-20-06)
1058:
Any person, affected by an order issued by the director may petition to the superior court for an injunction restraining the director from carrying out the provisions of the order and the court may, upon such petition, issue a temporary injunction restraining the director of community services pending the final disposition of the cause; provided, however, that such person shall present such petition to the court within fifteen (15) days of the posting and service of the order of the director. De novo hearings shall be had by the court on petitions within twenty (20) days. The court shall hear and determine the issues raised and shall enter such final order or decree as law and justice may requires; provided, however, that it shall not be necessary to file bond in any amount before obtaining a temporary injunction under this section.
(Ord. No. 001-06, § 1, 3-20-06)
1059:
Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as preventing the owner or owners of property from receiving just compensation for the taking of such property by the power of eminent domain under the laws of this state nor as permitting any property to be condemned or destroyed except in accordance with the police power of this state.
(Ord. No. 001-06, § 1, 3-20-06)
1060:
(a) The municipal court shall have full power and authority to order the abatement of any nuisance, whether public or private within the city, and the chief of police or public officer may execute the court's orders.
(b) When any public nuisance exists within the city, the director or chief of police or public officer on behalf of the public may file a complaint in the municipal court for abatement of such nuisance and the court shall cause reasonable notice of the time and place of the hearing to be given to the parties in interest.
(c) Any person creating or maintaining a nuisance within the city shall upon conviction thereof in the municipal court be punished as prescribed in section 1-1006 of this Code, and be required to abate such nuisance at his own expense, and if he fails to abate such nuisance within the time prescribed by the municipal court, it shall be abated by the public officer or the chief of police at the expense of the individual, firm, or corporation creating or maintaining the nuisance.
(d) For any amount expended by the city to abate a nuisance pursuant to a municipal court order, the city clerk shall issue an execution against the owner of the subject property if the owner fails to pay therefore when billed.

1062:
There is hereby established the East Point Clean Community Commission.

1065:
The commission shall consist of no more than twenty-five (25) members who shall be residents of East Point or designated resident or nonresident employees representing business or industry located within East Point, and who shall serve without remuneration. 1066:
The terms of office of members of the commission shall be for two (2) years each. (1) The city may acquire by eminent domain pursuant to applicable state law, any property determined to be vacant and a persistent nuisance, and shall have the power to hold, clear, manage or dispose of property so acquired for residential, commercial, industrial and related use.
(2) The city council shall not institute eminent domain proceedings pursuant to this section unless the director has certified that the property is vacant and a persistent nuisance. A property may only be certified to the city council as vacant and a persistent nuisance after the director has determined that:
(a) The owner of the property or designated agent has been sent a notice or order by the appropriate agency of the municipality to eliminate the conditions which are in violation of local codes or law;
(b) The property is vacant;
(c) The property is a persistent nuisance under the terms of this Chapter 4 of Part 7;
(d) The city has notified the property owner or designated agent that the property has been determined to be blighted or deteriorated and the time period for correction of such condition has expired and the property owner or agent has failed to comply with this notice.
(3) The findings required by subsection (2) shall be in writing and included in the report prepared by the director to the city council.
(4) The director shall notify the owner of the property or a designated agent that a determination that the property is vacant and a persistent nuisance has been made and that failure to eliminate the conditions causing such condition shall render the property subject to condemnation by the city under this part. Notice shall be mailed to the owner or designated agent by certified mail, return receipt requested. However, if the address of the owner or designated agent is unknown and cannot be ascertained by the commission in the exercise of reasonable diligence, copies of the notice shall be posted in a conspicuous place on the property affected and notice shall be published the newspaper which is the official organ of the county in which the sheriffs advertisements appear. The written notice sent to the owner or the owner's agent shall describe the conditions that render the property blighted and deteriorated, and shall demand abatement of the conditions within ninety (90) days of the receipt of such notice.
(5) An extension of the ninety-day time period may be granted by the city if the owner or designated agent demonstrates that such period is insufficient to correct the conditions cited in the notice.
(6) No elected official, officer or employee of the city shall acquire any interest in any property declared to be vacant or a persistent nuisance.
(7) If any elected official, officer or employee owns or has a financial interest, direct or indirect, in any property certified to be vacant and a persistent nuisance, the officer or employee shall immediately disclose, in writing, such interest to the city council, and such disclosure shall be entered in the minutes of the city council. Failure to so disclose such interest shall constitute misconduct in office.
(8) No payment shall be made to any elected official, officer or employee for any property or interest therein acquired by the city from such elected official, officer or employee unless the amount of such payment is fixed by court order in eminent domain proceedings, or unless payment is unanimously approved by the city council.

It shall be the duty of the city engineer to remove or cause to be removed, trees, the roots of which are breaking up sidewalks, street paving and street curbing, such roots to be removed also, at the expense of the owners thereof, unless such owners will permit the city engineer to remove such trees on behalf of the city without charging the city for such trees.
(Code 1959, § 19-34)
1121:
It shall be the duty of the city engineer to inspect the streets, street curbing and sidewalks of the city to determine where roots of trees are causing such street paving, street curbing, and sidewalks to be injured and to determine the ownership of such trees. In cases where the city owns the trees, they shall be removed by the city engineer, and in cases where such trees are not owned by the city, it shall be the duty of the city engineer to obtain, if he can, permission and authority from the owner of such tree to remove the same without expense to such owners, if such owners do not charge the city for such trees or for removing the same.
(Code 1959, § 19-35)
1122:
Where the owner of a tree, the roots of which are injuring the street paving or street curbing or sidewalk, will not permit or allow the city to remove such trees and such roots, it shall be the duty of the city engineer to forthwith notify the city attorney of such fact, in which notice the city engineer shall give the city attorney the specific location of such tree and the roots which are injuring the sidewalk, street paving or street curbing and the name of the street, and the name of the owner of the property with a brief description of such location of the owner's property, stating whether it is on the north side, east side, west side, or south side of the street, and the house number of such owner, if such owner is a resident of the city, and if not a resident of the city then such address as the city engineer is able to obtain.
(Code 1959, § 19-36)
1123:
Upon receiving the notice from the city engineer as prescribed in section 8-1037, it shall be the duty of the city attorney, the city engineer and the mayor to determine the value of such tree and the amount of the damage which would result to such owner's other property if such tree is condemned and removed, and thereupon to offer such owner the amount of such value and such damage, and upon the refusal of such owner to accept such amount, it shall be the duty of the city attorney to immediately institute condemnation proceedings for the purpose of condemning and removing such tree and to cause the proper amount to be paid to the clerk of the Superior Court of Fulton County when it has been determined as provided by law, whereupon it shall be the duty of the city engineer to forthwith remove such tree and its offending roots, and to keep record of the costs of such removal which are hereby assessed against such owner of such tree, and a bill for such costs shall be promptly presented to such owner; and on his refusal to pay the same promptly on demand by the city engineer, it shall be the duty of the city engineer to notify the city clerk of such fact, whereupon it shall be the duty of the city clerk to issue an execution for the amount of such cost against such owner and the real estate of such owner from which such tree was removed and place such execution in the hands of the city marshal for levy and sale; whereupon it shall be the duty of the city marshal to levy such execution or cause the same to be levied by a police officer upon such real estate of such owner. After advertisement once a week for four (4) weeks as in a tax advertisement for sale of real estate, it shall be the duty of such city marshal to sell such real estate to the highest bidder for cash in front of the council chamber on the first Tuesday in the month next succeeding the expiration of such four (4) weeks' advertising, and the purchaser of such sale shall have the same rights as in the case of a purchaser at a tax sale conducted by the city.
(Code 1959, § 19-37)
1124:
It shall be unlawful for anyone to obstruct or interfere with the city engineer or city marshal in the discharge of their duties under sections 8-1035 through 8-1038.
(Code 1959, § 19-38)
1125:
It shall be unlawful to have or maintain any hedge or shrubbery along any sidewalk or driveway where motor vehicles are used without keeping the hedges and shrubbery so trimmed and cut back that persons using such sidewalks can do so without injury from motor vehicles emerging from a driveway hidden behind a hedge or all shrubbery, whether the users of such sidewalk be children or adults.
(Code 1959, § 19-39)
1126:
It shall be responsibility of the community development department to notify the owner of every lot, improved or unimproved, having a hedge or shrubbery thereon in violation of section 8-1040 to comply with the provisions thereof, and if such owner fails or refuses to comply with such provisions within ten (10) days from the date of such notice, the city will cut or trim such hedge or shrubbery at the owner's expense, and will in addition, thereto prosecute such owner in the recorder's court for such offense.
(Ord. No. 927-86, § 1, 9-2-86)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 926-86, § 1 adopted Sept. 2, 1986, repealed former § 8-1041, relative to notification of violators of § 8-1040, which provisions derived from Code 1959, § 19-40. Ord. No. 927, § 1, adopted Sept. 2, 1986, enacted a new § 8-1041 to read as herein set out.
1127:
(a) It shall be the duty of every owner of any property within the city having hedge or shrubbery thereon, including growth, in violation of section 8-1040 to cut or trim the same to comply with such section within ten (10) days from the date notice to do so is served on such owner or the agent or tenant of such owner in possession of such property.
(b) No person shall be guilty of an offense under section 8-1040 for a violation of such section until the expiration of ten (10) days after service of such notice as provided in section 8-1041 of such violation.
(Code 1959, § 19-41)
1128:
It shall be the duty of the community development department to have cut or trimmed, by the building and grounds department, all hedges and shrubbery in violation of section 8-1040 at the owner's expense after expiration of such ten (10) days' time allowed for the owner to comply with the notice as prescribed in section 8-1041, and to bill the owner with the expense. If the bill is not paid in ten (10) days, it shall be the duty of the clerk of the city to issue an execution for the expense against such lot and the owner thereof, which execution shall be a lien against such lot and the owner thereof prior and superior to any and all other liens, except liens for taxes, and it shall be the duty of the city marshal to collect the execution by levy and sale of such lot, if it be not paid on demand as in case of tax executions of this city.
(Ord. No. 927, § 1, 9-2-86)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 926-86, § 1, adopted Sept. 2, 1986, repealed former § 8-1043, which pertained to when the chief of police to trim hedges or shrubbery in violation of § 8-1040 and levying costs therefore. Ord. No. 927, § 1, adopted Sept. 2, 1986 enacted a new § 8-1043 to read as herein set out.
1129:
It shall be unlawful for any lawn, yard or garden to be so laid out, planted, cultivated or maintained on any lot above or below the grade or level of the abutting street or sidewalk that the proper paving of the abutting street or sidewalk in the usual and ordinary manner will cause injury or damage to such yard, lawn, garden or flowers, which would not otherwise have occurred, or cause the abutting property to be washed away or to be flooded with surface water when heavy rains come, which washing or flooding would not have occurred otherwise.
(Code 1959, § 19-43)
1132:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to establish, locate, relocate, cut, lay out, construct, grade, pave, curb, widen or extend any public road, street, drive, walk, way, sewer or storm drain, which improvement is intended for or is likely to become a part of the city's highways, streets or roads, or which improvement is intended to be or is likely to be located within or become a part of a real estate subdivision or development within the city, without having first entered into an appropriate contract with the city, which has been approved by the city attorney and the city engineer. In the event the contract for such improvement is between a property owner or developer and the contractor, rather than the city, such contract shall be approved by the city engineer and city attorney.
(b) It shall be the duty of the city engineer to frequently visit, inspect, supervise and see that such work is done in accordance with such contract and the requirements of the city so that, upon completion thereof, he can make a certificate that he has inspected the work at every stage thereof, and that it has been done and completed in accordance with such requirements. No improvement shall be accepted by the city council without first receiving such certificate from the city engineer.
(c) It shall likewise be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to undertake any such improvement unless or until a satisfactory bond, with good and sufficient security, has been filed with the city purchasing agent and approved by the city attorney by the owner or person responsible for such improvement, whereby the city shall be adequately indemnified and protected against loss, injury or damage resulting from any failure to comply with any provision of this section, whether such failure be during the course of such undertaking or after its completion and the acceptance thereof by the city.
(Code 1959, § 19-44)
1133:
When an ordinance has been introduced to construct or repair a sanitary sewer, a sidewalk, or street curbing, or to pave or repair a street and all, or any part of the expense of such work or improvement is to be assessed against the abutting lands and owners thereof, notice thereof, and of the time and place of a public hearing thereon, shall be published one (1) time by the city clerk in the official newspaper of the city at least ten (10) but not more than thirty (30) days prior to the date of such hearing.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-44.01)
1134:
Any road or street which shall be hereafter proposed, planned, platted or constructed shall have a minimum width of thirty-two (32) feet from curb line to curb line, except that the city council may by resolution waive the aforementioned requirements to conform to the width of the street or road with other roads or streets with which it may connect or for any other reason which the city council may deem fit and proper.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-44.1)
1135:
It shall be unlawful for any person to commence construction upon any street or sidewalk in the city unless or until such person commencing such construction work has obtained and filed with the city adequate public liability insurance to protect and save the city harmless against loss, injury or damage on account of negligence of such person commencing such street or sidewalk construction, or satisfy the council that such public liability insurance has been obtained and is of full force and effect; provided, satisfactory proof that such public liability insurance has been obtained shall consist of a copy of the insurance policy or a certificate from the insurance company evidencing such fact.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-45)
1136:
The public liability insurance required by section 8-1064 shall be subject to the approval of the city council and will not be accepted or approved unless written by some insurance company authorized to write public liability insurance in this state and having an officer and agent located within the state.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-46)
1137:
The city engineer is hereby authorized and directed to approve and accept street and sidewalk paving and construction work and the construction of street curbing and the laying and constructing of sewers on behalf of the city, when and only when the work has been properly performed and completed in compliance with the contract, plans and specifications, where upon it shall be the duty of the city engineer to make and deliver to the city purchasing agent a certificate in which he shall certify that such contract and work thereunder have been properly executed and completed, and that it has been accepted on behalf of the city by the city engineer, and stating the unpaid amount of the contract price which is due and payable to the contractor, if such work has been done by a contractor; provided, it shall be the duty of the city engineer, on completion of any job, the cost of which or any part of the cost of which is to be assessed against abutting property owners, to furnish the city attorney with a copy of the certificate, in which certificate the city engineer shall certify the names of the abutting property owners and the lineal front footage to be assessed against each, with the amount to be assessed per lineal front foot, whereupon it shall be the duty of the city attorney to prepare and deliver unto the city council an ordinance assessing such costs as are assessable against such abutting properties and the owners thereof for action.
(Code 1959, § 19-48)
1138:
Any person desiring to cut or make any excavation in any street or paved sidewalk in the city for the purpose of making connections with sewer, water pipes, gas pipes or for any other purpose, shall before cutting or making any such excavation obtain a written permit from the director of public works. The application for such permit shall state the name of the person who expects to cut the street or sidewalk or make the excavation therein, for whom, and for what reason, and where, and the number of days required to do the work.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-48)
1139:
Any person who shall obtain a permit required by section 8-1067 shall thereby assume full responsibility for any loss or damage to the city or any person as a result of such excavation or other acts of negligence, and shall indemnify the city against any loss resulting from any damage to either person or property of any person, and any such permit shall contain this provision.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-49)
1140:
It shall be unlawful for any person, after having made an excavation in any street, to refill the same except under the immediate supervision and direction of the director of public works. It shall be the duty of any person making any such excavation to notify the city in writing when he shall have accomplished the work for which the excavation was made, and the city shall have the same refilled and the street restored to its former condition at the expense of the applicant.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-50)
1141:
It shall be the duty of the person making any excavation in any public street or place to maintain a signal at the place of excavation by keeping a red light burning at same from sundown to sunrise and red flag during the day.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-51)
1142:
When any sidewalk or street is about to be paved it shall be the duty of the director of public works to notify in writing all of the owners of the abutting lots on such street requiring them to have made at their expense all necessary sewer, gas and water stub-outs from the sewer, gas and water mains to their respective property lines within five (5) days from the date of such notice.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-52)
1143:
Any person failing to make all necessary sewer, gas and water stub-outs from the sewer, gas and water mains to their respective properties when duly notified to do so shall, in the event such person should desire water, sewer or gas connections made to his premises after the pavement has been laid, be charged a fee in connection therewith, in addition to ordinary and other costs of such connections or stubouts for entering the pavement, if such connection is made within five (5) years from the date the street is paved.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-53)
1144:
A charge, as determined by city council shall be assessed, levied and charged against owners of lands abutting a street right-of-way (except the City of East Point) for engineering services necessary in making profiles for street curbing and guttering on both sides of a street, and the amount estimated in advance by the city engineer as necessary to pay such costs in each case shall be deposited in advance with said city engineer before such service is rendered by said city for any private person, firm, corporation or association.
(Code 1959, Sec. 19-53.1)
1147:
All public sidewalks and those parts of all private driveways which are within the sidewalk or street area shall be laid and constructed according to specifications of the city, and shall be constructed and laid by the public works department, or by contract subject to final approval by the city, and it shall be unlawful for any sidewalk or private driveway within the sidewalk or street area to be constructed otherwise.
(Code 1959, § 19-54)
1148:
All future private driveway approaches from public streets of the city shall be paved according to city driveway construction specifications within such street right-of-way.
(Code 1959, § 19-54.1)
1149:
To secure uniformity of construction and compliance with city driveway construction specifications, all future construction of private driveway approaches from a public street, and within the street right-of-way, shall be performed at the expense of the owner of the lot to the driveway of which such approaches are constructed, but only after written permission shall have been obtained from the city engineer to whom application for such permission shall be made in writing accompanied by a set of plans and specifications approved in writing by said city engineer, in which application for such permission the applicant shall covenant and agree to construct such private driveway approaches in accordance with such plans and specifications.
(Code 1959, § 19-54.2)
1150: It shall be lawful for the owner of any lot desiring to construct a driveway into such lot from an abutting public street to construct the same or have it constructed provided a permit to construct the same is granted by the city engineer; provided, further, that such permit shall not be granted by the city engineer unless nor until he shall have approved written plans and specifications submitted in duplicate to him with a written application for such permit in which application the owner or applicant for such permit shall covenant and agree to construct such driveway in accordance with such approved plans and specification; provided, further, that upon completion such construction shall be subject to approval by the city engineer of the city, and shall not be open for use unless nor until the same shall have received such approval of the city engineer, of which completion the city engineer shall be promptly notified, so that the city engineer can inspect the same for the purpose of determining whether the construction has been completed in accordance with the plans and specifications previously approved by him.
1151:
When it shall be lawful for anyone other than the city to lay down, open, grade, pave or construct any public street or sidewalk, any person desiring to grade or pave any sidewalk shall first make application in writing to the city engineer and obtain a written permit for doing such work, and also obtain specifications, line and grade as to the manner in which such sidewalks shall be graded and paved and the kind and proportions of material to be used in the paving of same and the width and other dimensions of the sidewalk or curb. All of such work shall be subject to the approval of the city engineer.
(Code 1959, § 19-55)
1152:
Any person grading, paving or changing the condition of any sidewalk or curb shall first apply in writing to the city engineer and obtain the proper line and grade for such sidewalk or curb, and the city shall have a reasonable length of time in which to furnish the same.
(Code 1959, § 19-56)
1153:
No permit issued under the provisions of section 8-1095 shall be valid unless the work for which same is issued shall be completed within thirty (30) days from the date of the issuance of the permit therefor.
(Code 1959, § 19-57)
1154:
The city may in its discretion refuse to give the line or grade for any curb or sidewalk within the limits of the city, in which case the sidewalk or curbing shall not be molested.
(Code 1959, § 19-58)
1155:
The director of public works shall have supervision over sidewalks and curbing and shall see that any person changing the condition of any sidewalk or curb shall have obtained the proper permit, line, grade and specifications and before accepting any sidewalk or curb work shall determine that the proper line, grade and specifications have been complied with.
(Code 1959, § 19-59; Ord. No. 877-85, § 1, 3-4-85)

1160:
The City of East Point shall provide water, electricity, sanitation and sewer services to its residents and businesses as provided herein, unless said resident or business is eligible to choose its service provider as allowed by state or federal laws or regulations. Entities outside the city limits may be provided any or all such services on a contractual basis with any such contracts approved by city council.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1161:
Customer. Customers shall include any and all individuals, commercial entities or industries that obtain from the City of East Point retail electrical, water, sanitation and sewer services.
(a) Residential customers shall include individuals who own or rent a single-family residence, whether it is a house, an apartment, a condominium, a mobile home or any other structure permitted for residential dwelling.
(b) Commercial customers shall include any business or corporate entity.
(c) Industrial customers shall include entities meeting such criteria as shall be established by the city in writing from time to time.
Cut-off shall refer to the termination of service to a customer as provided for in section 8-2011.
Deposit shall refer to the deposit required of customers in section 8-2012 below.
Due date shall refer to the due date described in subsection 8-2009(e) below.
Late fee shall refer to the late fee described in subsection 8-2009(f) below.
Payment plan shall refer to a negotiated term through Customer Care to pay a specific utility bill over a period, not to exceed twelve (12) months.
Payment arrangement shall refer to a negotiated arrangement to pay a specific utility bill in full within thirty (30) days of its due date.
Reconnect fee shall refer to the reconnect fee described in subsection 8-2011(d) below.
Substantial improvements shall refer to any rehabilitation or remodeling to a residential unit that requires a permit from planning and zoning and is an alteration, modification or repair impacting at least twenty-five (25) percent or more of the residential unit.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1162:
Any person receiving utility service from the city shall execute and comply with all rules and regulations of the city regarding the use of utilities.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1163:
For each new utility customer or where service is rebuilt or relocated for the convenience of or at the request of the customer, installation and connection charges shall be paid by the customer. The charges shall be recommended by staff and approved by the city council. Said charges shall be posted in Customer Care department and on the city website. Said charges shall be in addition to any other charges levied for provision of service.
(a) The city shall furnish electric meters and the customer shall furnish the electrical receptacles and water meters and receptacles shall be furnished as specified in subsections 8-2004 (e through k) below.
(b) No charge shall be incurred for normal maintenance or repair associated due to normal wear and age, provided that such repairs are acknowledged by public utilities as part of the city's normal maintenance responsibility.
(c) All meters shall be the sole property of the city and complete ownership and control of the meters shall be vested in the city. The city reserves the right in the event of actual or threatened power failure or safety hazard to make repairs of a permanent or temporary nature on the meters. No meter shall be tampered with or altered in a manner as to affect the safety, convenience, adequacy or the accuracy of the metering service in any manner, direct or indirect.
(d) If any materials or work associated with the customer's service installation are provided by the customer, such materials and/or work shall conform to the specifications and requirements as established by the city in writing from time to time.
(e) The service line from the water main to the meter box and three (3) feet beyond is type "K" soft copper. All connections on copper services shall be flared or compression type. The water and sewer department shall approve any exceptions in advance.
(f) All water main taps will be the same size or larger than the service line and meter. Multiple smaller, taps manifold together to achieve an equivalent tap size is not allowed. For taps larger than two (2) inches in diameter, a tapping sleeve and valve are required. The tapping sleeve shall be per the City of East Point Water and Sewer Department standard specifications.
(g) All meters are required to be of the type and brand as approved by the water and sewer department. All water meters less than two (2) inches shall be purchased from the city in addition to the water tap fee unless the water user is constructing a new development serving seven (7) or more residential customers. The property owner or water user shall purchase and install all other meters two (2) inches and above. The water and sewer department shall approve the type of meter such as turbine, compound, etc. All meters larger than two (2) inches shall be installed with the appropriate valves and a bypass, where, in the judgment of the water and sewer department, uninterruptible service is mandated and/or important.
(h) City policy is that a tap fee is due any time a new service tap or connection is made to the city's water main. This includes location where taps have previously been made and have been or are being abandoned. The city may waive the tap or connection fee at its discretion in cases where the existing tap is being abandoned and the location of the new tap is to the city's benefit. In all cases, a plumbing permit and, if applicable, a street cut permit are required.
(i) Meters shall be at least eighteen (18) inches and not more than thirty (30) inches in the ground. If a change in grade of the yard, parking or sidewalk is made the service line and meter shall be changed to correspond with this requirement.
(j) Although the city does not make taps larger than one (1) inch in diameter for water services, it is required, by state law, to inspect them. It is the contractor's responsibility to notify the water and sewer department directly. A tapping inspector from the water and sewer department shall be present before and during the actual cutting of the tap. If a tap is made before the water and sewer department inspector arrives, this will be a code violation. It is crucial for the inspector to observe that the tap coupon and cutting are recovered and not lost into the water main. The inspector shall further check the construction of the service line from the water main to the meter and the meter installation to ensure compliance with city codes. The contractor, prior to inspection, shall not cover any connections or fittings.
(k) The property owner or water user shall be responsible for the purchase of their required water meter. The customer shall purchase water meters less than two (2) inches and boxes from the City of East Point only if the water meter is being installed by the city. The city will install service tap, meter and meter box for any residential water meter ranging in size from five-eighth (⅝) inch to one and one-half (1½) inches serving residential customers and where one meter per residential customer is installed not to exceed six (6) total meters.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1164:
All utility meters for the measurement of electricity or water supplied by the city shall be installed outdoors. Electric meters shall be located on the property at a distance of four (4) feet above the ground. When outside installation is impractical, other installations may be made with standard meter sockets at acceptable locations with the permission of the city.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1165:
(a) Owners of all new multi-family residential dwellings or complexes or any unit permitted for a substantial improvement shall install separate electric meters for each individual dwelling unit. If an owner of multi-family dwelling or complex fails to install such separate electric meter for each individual dwelling unit, the electric service to such customer at said address shall be discontinued until such property owner complies with the requirements of this section.
(b) All new multi-family residential dwellings, apartments, townhomes, condominiums, mobile home parks shall be built with individual water utility owned meters on each unit or sub-unit meters owned and managed by the property owner with a utility owned master meter that bills for water service based on volume of use for each customer. The billing for water use can be accomplished by the water provider or by a private, third party, such as the development owner, if conditions are met and approved by the water and sewer department director. If existing city owned rights-of-way are not suitable for the installation of individual meters, the following conditions must be met for the installation of individual meters on private property:
(1) The owners of all individual living units shall grant easements to the city for meter installation within ten feet of the curb line of existing rights-of-way for water mains.
(2) The easements shall comply with the specifications then in force of the department of water.
(3) The owner of all individual living units shall sign an agreement indemnifying the city from any and all damage claims resulting from the installation, maintenance of and access to meters on private property.
(4) The owner of each individual living premises shall sign a written acknowledgment that water lines between the meter and living unit and the living unit interior plumbing will be maintained by the owner and that cutoff valves must be installed by the owner on the discharge side of the meter box at or near the property line.
(5) If required in lieu of dedicated streets, a twenty-foot right-of-way centered on the water main shall be conveyed to the city, except that the director of the water and sewer department may accept a narrower right-of-way where obstructions are involved.
If an owner of multi-family dwelling or complex fails to install such separate water meter for each individual dwelling unit, the water service to such customer at said address shall be discontinued until such property owner complies with the requirements of this section.
(c) All substantial improvements to multi-family buildings (i.e. apartments, townhomes, condominiums and mobile home parks) shall require the installation of individual water utility owned meters on each unit or sub-unit meters owned and managed by the property owner with a utility owned master meter that bills for water service based on volume of use for each customer. The billing for water use can be accomplished by the water provider or by a private, third party, such as the development owner, if conditions are met and approved by the water and sewer department. If an owner of multi-family dwelling or complex fails to install such separate water meter for each individual dwelling unit, the water service to such customer at said address shall be discontinued until such property owner complies with the requirements of this section.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1166:
Water accounts will be charged only to the property that the meter serves directly and to the owner or his authorized agent, such as a tenant with a valid lease or management company under contract. Liens for unpaid water accounts may be placed on the property pursuant to subsection 8-2009(i) only if the charges were incurred by the property owner.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1167:
(a) Initiation and deposits. All prospective customers shall apply for utility service in person or by mail. Proof of East Point residency or current business license must be provided. A deposit for service will be required to initiate service of all customers in addition to a connection fee. The prospective customer will undergo and pay the city for a credit check to determine the amount of deposit required unless the customer opts to pay the highest amount. The deposit schedule shall be posted in Customer Care and on the city's website. The charge per credit check to the prospective customer shall be established by Customer Care.
(b) Reserved.
(c) Past due accounts. In the event there are any outstanding utility bills due from the prospective customer, no service may be initiated until all amounts due have been paid.
(d) Property deficiencies. In the event the subject address is on the list of properties being condemned by the city or no certificate of occupancy has been issued for the service address, utility service may not be initiated until the customer has addressed the specific problems with the city and a statement is provided in writing that utility service may be initiated.
(e) The city will use its current financial institution or the credit rating agency issuing the credit score to determine three credit levels. The minimum score for "good" credit, the minimum score for "medium" credit and the maximum score for "bad" credit shall be determined by the customer care director.
(f) Deposits will be charged at the following levels:
(1) "Good" credit score = One hundred dollars ($100.00);
(2) "Medium" credit score = One hundred fifty dollars ($150.00);
(3) "Bad" credit score = Two hundred dollars ($200.00).
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1168:
All bills for utility services, including but not limited to electricity, water, sewer, garbage, sanitation, and security lights, are due and payable in full upon receipt.
(a) Rates. All rates for utility services shall be recommended by staff and approved by the city council. Said rate structure and tables shall be available for inspection at city hall and on the East Point website.
(b) Statements. Utility bills shall include charges for electricity, water, sewer, storm water and sanitation. Statements shall include the following information:
(1) The date of the utility bill;
(2) The time period for the services covered by the utility bill;
(3) The utility charges and/or installment and surcharge due;
(4) The date when the payment is due in full;
(5) Notice of whether the utility bill is based on an actual or estimated measurement of the amount of utility service supplied;
(6) Notice of any past due amounts.
(c) Payment location. Bills shall be paid in person or by mail at the location(s) specified by Customer Care, or if such service is available, bills may be paid on-line.
(d) Method of payment. Bills may be paid in cash, by money order, cashier's check or personal check. If a customer has had a check for payment of a utility bill returned by the bank for nonpayment, account closed, payment stopped, or similar reasons two (2) or more times in a twelve-month period, a personal check will not be accepted for the next twelve-month period. Any check so returned by the bank or credit union shall render the account as 'unpaid' and the city's approved returned check fee will be charged to the customer along with any late fees.
(e) Due date. All utility bills must be paid by the twenty-first (21st) day (the "due date") following the billing date.
(f) Late fee. Customers who have not paid their bills by the due date shall pay a late fee in addition to payment of the total amount of the utility bill beginning on the twenty-second (22nd) day following the billing date. Said fee shall be proposed by Customer Care, and upon approval by the city council, shall be posted in a public place in Customer Care and on the city's website.
(g) Budget billing. Residential customers with no delinquent payments in their payment record for a one-year period may chose the budget billing option for payment of electric services. Under this option, the customer's charge ("budget billing payment") for monthly electricity during the next subsequent twelve-month period shall be based upon an average of monthly charges for the preceding twelve-month period ("prior average payment"). The budget billing payment shall be calculated by the city annually for each customer that elects to use the budget billing option. The budget billing payment shall be a calculation of the prior average payment modified for collection of any previous accumulated budget difference plus estimated rate and use increases or decreases identified by Customer Care. In the event the customer moves out of the city or elects to terminate budget billing, the customer shall owe the city any accumulated budget difference ("deficit") between the actual and the budget billing. In case of a surplus accumulation ("surplus"), the city shall apply the surplus to the next actual billing until used or reimburse the customer when service is completely terminated. In the event the customer elects to renew budget billing for an additional annual term, any deficit or surplus from the previous term will be applied to the new budget billing payment for collection during the new term.
(h) Billing for multi-family dwelling or complex. All existing multi-family buildings (i.e. apartments, townhomes, condominiums, mobile home parks) with a utility owned master meter shall be billed for a monthly minimum charge on each single family residential unit, (total number of units will be determined by the plat submitted and approved by planning and zoning) whether occupied or not, located upon the multiple residential premises, plus any excess water used above the calculated minimum charge. To the extent the owner of the multi-family dwelling unit does not desire to be billed for condemned units, such owner must provide Customer Care with a copy of a certificate of condemnation for such unit along with a copy of the plan for rehabilitation or demolishment pursuant to section 7-8002 of the City of East Point Code of Ordinances. Whenever it is necessary for Customer Care to notify the residents of a multi-family dwelling of pending termination of services due to non-payment of water and sewer bills, a charge of one dollar ($1.00) per residential unit will be assessed against the account in order to recover the associated administrative costs incurred by the city.
(i) Unpaid utility charges. After a utility account has remained unpaid for one hundred twenty (120) days or more, there shall be an automatic lien on the property for unpaid utility charges when such property owner has incurred the unpaid utility charges.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1169:

(a) Charge for rereading a meter;
(b) Charge for calibration of a meter;
(c) Charge for disconnecting/reconnecting services at customer's request; and
(d) Charge for relocating poles and service connections at the customer's request.
If, upon the provision of the special service, a correction is determined necessary through no fault of the customer, the special service fee shall be waived or credited to the customer's account. In addition, the customer may appeal any inappropriate charges for utility services to Customer Care. Any credits due the customer by the city shall be applied to the customer's account.

1170:
(a) Termination notice. Each customer must notify the city in person or in writing that their utility service is to be terminated at their residence or business at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance and a final bill shall be issued upon the termination of service. Said final bill is due and payable upon receipt.
(b) Reserved.
(c) Cut-off of utilities. Upon the twenty-ninth (29th) day (the "cut-off") from the billing date, utility service may be disconnected at any time.
(d) Reestablishing service and reconnect fee. In order to reestablish service, a customer must pay in person the reconnect fee, delinquent amount, the late fee and any returned check fee. Said reconnect fee shall be recommended by staff, approved by city council and posted in a public place in Customer Care and on the City of East Point website.
(e) Error in cut-off. If the utility service is cut off in error by the cty, the customer shall receive a credit of any fees paid in error and be awarded a twenty-five dollar ($25.00) credit to be applied to the customer's account. If no objection is made to the twenty-five dollar ($25.00) credit within thirty (30) days of its issuance, it shall be deemed full and final settlement for any and all alleged damages flowing from such error.
(f) Hardship. In the event a customer is unable to pay a utility bill in full due to a hardship, Customer Care may halt the disconnection of utilities based on any of the following:
(1) Medical. The customer must be pre-registered with written confirmation by his or her doctor for the need to sustain life on life-support equipment (i.e. - oxygen tank) to any member of the household. The city shall confirm the existence of the equipment by an inspection of the premises. The maximum time for a medical hold shall be sixty (60) days.
(2) Financial. A customer in good standing may request either a payment plan or a payment arrangement through Customer Care. To be in good standing, a customer must have had no more than one (1) check returned in the preceding twelve (12) months and must not have been disconnected for non-payment during that same time period. A payment plan may be granted every six (6) months upon a finding of good cause by Customer Care and to the extent there is not already an outstanding payment plan. A payment arrangement may be granted up to three (3) times a year. Customer Care shall exercise discretion and sound business judgment in the granting of both payment plans and payment arrangements and should consider such additional factors such as employment, frequency of requests and prior performance under any prior payment agreement or payment plan and any other relevant objective factors. Any such payment plan or payment arrangement shall not relieve the customer from the timely payment of all subsequent monthly utility payments.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1171:
Advance deposits for utility service will first be applied to any outstanding balance due on the account and only after such deduction shall any credit balance will be refunded to the customer.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)
1172:
Whenever utilities are discontinued for any reason, it shall be unlawful for any person except an authorized agent or employee of the city to restore such service or to make meter connection or disconnection except by a duly authorized agent of the city performing their duty. Any customer who reconnects the power or water after disconnection in violation of this section shall be assessed a fee of one hundred dollars ($100.00) for the cost of pulling that customer's meter to prevent further unauthorized connections. Any customer who continues in the unauthorized use of service, receipt of unauthorized electric service or who creates a hazardous condition as a result of their unauthorized connection shall be assessed a fee of two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) as the fee to cover the cost of disconnecting the customer from the electrical utility pole or water main. 1173:
(a) At any time before the date of termination of utility service for nonpayment of the amount(s) shown on a utility bill, a notice of rejection or a notice of termination, a residential customer may dispute the correctness of all or part of the amount(s) shown in accordance with the provisions of this article. A residential customer shall not be entitled to dispute the correctness of all or part of the amount(s) if all or part of the amount(s) was (were) the subject of a previous dispute under this section.
(b) The procedure for residential customer disputes shall be as follows:
(1) Before the date of termination, the residential customer shall notify Customer Care, orally or in writing, that he disputes all or part of the amount(s) shown on a utility bill, a notice of rejection or a notice of termination, stating as completely as possible the basis for the dispute.
(2) If Customer Care determines that the present dispute is untimely or that the residential customer previously disputed the correctness of all or part of the amount(s) shown, Customer Care department shall mail to the customer a notice stating that the present dispute is untimely or invalid. Customer Care shall then proceed as if the customer had not notified the utility of the present dispute.
(3) If Customer Care determines that the present dispute is not untimely or invalid under this section, Customer Care, within three (3) days after receipt of the customer's notice, shall arrange an informal meeting between the residential customer and Customer Care.
(4) Based on the utility's records, the customer's allegations and all other relevant materials available to the official, Customer Care shall resolve the dispute, attempting to do so in a manner satisfactory to both.
(5) Within five (5) days of completion of the meeting, Customer Care shall mail to the customer a copy of his decision resolving the dispute, unless at the time of the hearing the customer is notified in writing of the decision.
(6) If the decision is unsatisfactory to the customer, the customer, within three (3) business days of his receipt of the official's decision, may request, in writing, a formal hearing before Customer Care.
(7) The formal hearing before Customer Care shall be held within ten (10) days of the utility's receipt of the customer's written request.
(8) At the hearing, Customer Care and the customer shall be entitled to present all evidence that is, in Customer Care's view, relevant and material to the dispute and to examine and cross-examine witnesses.
(9) Based on the record established at the hearing, Customer Care, within five (5) days of the completion of the hearing, shall issue a written decision formally resolving the dispute and it shall be final and binding on the utility and the customer.
(c) Utilization of this dispute procedure shall not relieve a residential customer of his obligation to timely and completely pay all other undisputed utility charges and/or installments and surcharges, and the undisputed portion(s) of the amount(s) which is (are) the subject of the present dispute. Failure to timely and completely pay all such undisputed amounts shall subject the customer to termination of utility service in accordance with the provisions of this article.
(d) Until the date of the hearing with Customer Care, the customer must make full payment of the disputed amount unless, after a determination of good cause by Customer Care, it is proper for the customer to suspend payment until the hearings are complete.
(Ord. No. 007-13, 3-18-13)

(a) All new utility services to commercial and industrial establishments shall be assessed a charge for the installation of facilities and instruments for electric service equal to the actual cost that shall include labor (including administrative costs), equipment, materials and/or contract services to complete the service connection.

1178:
This division shall be known as the Identity Theft Prevention Program.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 1, 10-20-08)
1179:
The purpose of this division is to comply with 16 CFR § 681.2 in order to detect, prevent and mitigate identity theft by identifying and detecting identity theft red flags and by responding to such red flags in a manner that will prevent identity theft.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 1, 10-20-08)
1180:
For purposes of this division, the following definitions apply:
(a) City means the City of East Point.
(b) Covered account means (i) An account that a financial institution or creditor offers or maintains, primarily for personal, family, or household purposes, that involves or is designed to permit multiple payments or transactions, such as a credit card account, mortgage loan, automobile loan, margin account, cell phone account, utility account, checking account, or savings account; and (ii) any other account that the financial institution or creditor offers or maintains for which there is a reasonably foreseeable risk to customers or to the safety and soundness of the financial institution or creditor from identity theft, including financial, operational, compliance, reputation, or litigation risks.
(c) Credit means the right granted by a creditor to a debtor to defer payment of debt or to incur debts and defer its payment or to purchase property or services and defer payment therefore.
(d) Creditor means any person who regularly extends, renews, or continues credit; any person who regularly arranges for the extension, renewal, or continuation of credit; or any assignee of an original creditor who participates in the decision to extend, renew, or continue credit and includes utility companies and telecommunications companies.
(e) Customer means a person that has a covered account with a creditor.
(f) Identity theft means a fraud committed or attempted using identifying information of another person without authority.
(g) Person means a natural person, a corporation, government or governmental subdivision or agency, trust, estate, partnership, cooperative, or association.
(h) Personal identifying information means a person's credit card account information, debit card information bank account information and drivers' license information and for a natural person includes their social security number, mother's birth name, and date of birth.
(i) Red flag means a pattern, practice, or specific activity that indicates the possible existence of identity theft.
(j) Service provider means a person that provides a service directly to the city.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 1, 10-20-08)
1181:
(1) The city is a creditor pursuant to 16 CFR § 681.2 due to its provision or maintenance of covered accounts for which payment is made in arrears.
(2) Covered accounts offered to customers for the provision of city services include utility accounts such as water, sewer, sanitation and electric services.
(3) The processes of opening a new covered account, restoring an existing covered account, and making payments on such accounts that have been identified as potential processes in which identity theft could occur.
(4) The city limits access to personal identifying information to those employees responsible for or otherwise involved in opening or restoring covered accounts or accepting payment for use of covered accounts. Information provided to such employees is entered directly into the city's computer system and is not otherwise recorded.
(5) The city determines that there is a moderate risk of identity theft occurring in the following ways (if any):
(a) Use by an applicant of another person's personal identifying information to establish a new covered account;
(b) Use of a previous customer's personal identifying information by another person in an effort to have service restored in the previous customer's name;
(c) Use of another person's credit card, bank account, or other method of payment by a customer to pay such customer's covered account or accounts; and
(d) Use by a customer desiring to restore such customer's covered account of another person's credit card, bank account, or other method of payment.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 1, 10-20-08)
1182:
(1) As a precondition to opening a covered account in the city, each applicant shall provide the city with personal identifying information of the customer a valid government issued identification card containing a photograph of the customer or, for customers who are not natural persons, a photograph of the customer's agent opening the account. "Such applicant shall also provide any information necessary for the department providing the service for which the covered account is created to access the applicant's consumer credit report". Such information shall be entered directly into the city's computer system and shall not otherwise be recorded.
(2) Each account shall be assigned an account number and personal identification number (PIN) which shall be unique to that account. The city may utilize computer software to randomly generate assigned PINs and to encrypt account numbers and PINs.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 1, 10-20-08)
1183:
(1) Access to customer accounts shall be password protected and shall be limited to authorized city personnel.
(2) Such password(s) shall be changed by the director of information technology on a regular basis, shall be at least eight (8) characters in length and shall contain letters, numbers and symbols.
(3) Any unauthorized access to or other breach of customer accounts is to be reported immediately to the city manager and the password changed immediately.
(4) Personal identifying information included in customer accounts is considered confidential and any request or demand for such information shall be immediately forwarded to the city manager and the city attorney.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 1, 10-20-08)
1184:
(1) In the event that credit card payments that are made over the Internet are processed through a third party service provider, such third party service provider shall certify that it has an adequate identity theft prevention program in place that is applicable to such payments.
(2) All credit card payments made over the telephone or the city's website shall be entered directly into the customer's account information in the computer data base.
(3) Account statements and receipts for covered accounts shall include only the last four digits of the credit or debit card or the bank account used for payment of the covered account.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 1, 10-20-08)
1185:
All employees responsible for or involved in the process of opening a covered account, restoring a covered account or accepting payment for a covered account shall check for red flags as indicators of possible identity theft and such red flags may include:
(1) Alerts from consumer reporting agencies, fraud detection agencies or service providers. Examples of alerts include but are not limited to:
a. A fraud or active duty alert that is included with a consumer report;
b. A notice of credit freeze in response to a request for a consumer report;
c. A notice of address discrepancy provided by a consumer reporting agency;
d. Indications of a pattern of activity in a consumer report that is inconsistent with the history and usual pattern of activity of an applicant or customer, such as:
i. A recent and significant increase in the volume of inquiries;
ii. An unusual number of recently established credit relationships;
iii. A material change in the use of credit, especially with respect to recently established credit relationships; or
iv. An account that was closed for cause or identified for abuse of account privileges by a financial institution or creditor.
(2) Suspicious documents. Examples of suspicious documents include:
a. Documents provided for identification that appear to be altered or forged;
b. Identification on which the photograph or physical description is inconsistent with the appearance of the applicant or customer;
c. Identification on which the information is inconsistent with information provided by the applicant or customer;
d. Identification on which the information is inconsistent with readily accessible information that is on file with the financial institution or creditor, such as a signature card or a recent check; or
e. An application that appears to have been altered or forged, or appears to have been destroyed and reassembled.
(3) Suspicious personal identification, such as suspicious address change. Examples of suspicious identifying information include:
a. Personal identifying information that is inconsistent with external information sources used by the financial institution or creditor. For example:
i. The address does not match any address in the consumer report; or
ii. The Social Security Number (SSN) has not been issued, or is listed on the Social Security Administration's Death Master File.
b. Personal identifying information provided by the customer is not consistent with other personal identifying information provided by the customer, such as a lack of correlation between the SSN range and date of birth.
c. Personal identifying information or a phone number or address, is associated with known fraudulent applications or activities as indicated by internal or third-party sources used by the financial institution or creditor.
d. Other information provided, such as fictitious mailing address, mail drop addresses, jail addresses, invalid phone numbers, pager numbers or answering services, is associated with fraudulent activity.
e. The SSN provided is the same as that submitted by other applicants or customers.
f. The address or telephone number provided is the same as or similar to the account number or telephone number submitted by an unusually large number of applicants or customers.
g. The applicant or customer fails to provide all required personal identifying information on an application or in response to notification that the application is incomplete.
h. Personal identifying information is not consistent with personal identifying information that is on file with the financial institution or creditor.
i. The applicant or customer cannot provide authenticating information beyond that which generally would be available from a wallet or consumer report.
(4) Unusual use of or suspicious activity relating to a covered account. Examples of suspicious activity include:
a. Shortly following the notice of a change of address for an account, city receives a request for the addition of authorized users on the account.
b. A new revolving credit account is used in a manner commonly associated with known patterns of fraud patterns. For example:
i. The customer fails to make the first payment or makes an initial payment but no subsequent payments.
c. An account is used in a manner that is not consistent with established patterns of activity on the account. There is, for example:
i. Nonpayment when there is no history of late or missed payments;
ii. A material change in purchasing or spending patterns;
d. An account that has been inactive for a long period of time is used (taking into consideration the type of account, the expected pattern of usage and other relevant factors).
e. Mail sent to the customer is returned repeatedly as undeliverable although transactions continue to be conducted in connection with the customer's account.
f. The city is notified that the customer is not receiving paper account statements.
g. The city is notified of unauthorized charges or transactions in connection with a customer's account.
h. The city is notified by a customer, law enforcement or another person that it has opened a fraudulent account for a person engaged in identity theft.
(5) Notice from customers, law enforcement, victims or other reliable sources regarding possible identity theft or phishing relating to covered accounts.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 1, 10-20-08)
1188:
The director of finance is responsible for oversight of the program and for program implementation. The city manager is responsible for reviewing reports prepared by staff regarding compliance with red flag requirements and with recommending material changes to the program, as necessary in the opinion of the city manager, to address changing identity theft risks and to identify new or discontinued types of covered accounts. Any recommended material changes to the program shall be submitted to the city council for consideration by the council.
(1) The director of finance will report to the city manager at least annually, on compliance with the red flag requirements. The report will address material matters related to the program and evaluate issues such as:
a. The effectiveness of the policies and procedures of city in addressing the risk of identity theft in connection with the opening of covered accounts and with respect to existing covered accounts;
b. Service provider arrangements;
c. Significant incidents involving identity theft and management's response; and

The director of finance shall exercise his or her discretion in determining the amount and substance of training necessary.

1189:
In the event that the city engages a service provider to perform an activity in connection with one or more covered accounts the Director of Finance shall exercise his or her discretion in reviewing such arrangements in order to ensure, to the best of his or her ability, that the service provider's activities are conducted in accordance with policies and procedures, agreed upon by contract, that are designed to detect any red flags that may arise in the performance of the service provider's activities and take appropriate steps to prevent or mitigate identity theft.

1192:
This division shall be know as Treatment of Address Discrepancies.

1193:
Pursuant to 16 CFR § 681.1, the purpose of this division is to establish a process by which the city will be able to form a reasonable belief that a consumer report relates to the consumer about whom it has requested a consumer credit report when the city has received a notice of address discrepancy.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 2, 10-20-08)
1194:
For purposes of this division, the following definitions apply:
(1) Notice of address discrepancy means a notice sent to a user by a consumer reporting agency pursuant to 15 U.S.C. § 1681(c)(h)(1), that informs the user of a substantial difference between the address for the consumer that the user provided to request the consumer report and the address(es) in the agency's file for the consumer.
(2) City means the City of East Point, Georgia.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 2, 10-20-08)
1195:
In the event that the city receives a notice of address discrepancy, the city employee responsible for verifying consumer addresses for the purpose of providing the municipal service or account sought by the consumer shall perform one or more of the following activities, as determined to be appropriate by such employee:
(1) Compare the information in the consumer report with:
a. Information the city obtains and uses to verify a consumer's identity in accordance with the requirements of the Customer Information Program rules implementing 31 U.S.C. § 5318(1);
b. Information the city maintains in its own records, such as applications for service, change of address notices, other customer account records or tax records; or
c. Information the city obtains from third-party sources that are deemed reliable by the relevant city employee; or
(2) Verify the information in the consumer report with the consumer.

1196:

This information is required to be provided to the consumer reporting agency when:
a. The city is able to form a reasonable belief that the consumer report relates to the consumer about whom the city requested the report;

1197:
The city employee charged with confirming consumer addresses may, in his or her discretion, confirm the accuracy of an address through one or more of the following methods:
(1) Verifying the address with the consumer;
(2) Reviewing the city's records to verify the consumer's address.
(Ord. No. 030-08, § 2, 10-20-08)

1200:
(a) Power cost adjustment: Power cost adjustment shall mean that increase or decrease in rates charged to customers of the city's electric utility sufficient for the city to recover total electric utility costs, including but not limited to wholesale power cost, investment in future energy resources, costs of distribution system operation and maintenance, administrative costs attributable to utility operations, and transfers and allocations paid to the city. Rates charged to electric utility customers may be increased or decreased in an amount per kilowatt hour (kWh) through a power cost adjustment rider. In keeping with sound financial management practices, the policy of the city will be to ensure that its utilities are operated in a fiscally sound manner and as such to make power cost adjustments to pass on increased operating, maintenance and capital costs to utility customers as needed.
(b) Power cost adjustment rider (PCA): The monthly power cost adjustment in cents per kWh shall represent the difference between total electric department costs (including wholesale power, distribution system operation & maintenance, administrative charges, transfers and allocations paid to the general fund of the City of East Point) and total electric department revenues (including sales of electricity and other operating receipts) divided by the total kilowatt hour sold to customers served under tariffs subject to such power cost adjustment (PCA). Application of this rider is at the sole discretion of the City of East Point. Applicable tariffs include residential, general service, small power, medium power, and large power.
(c) Environmental compliance cost: The environmental compliance cost shall mean that increase or decrease in rates charged to customers of the city's electric utility sufficient for the city to recover capital costs and operating and maintenance costs associated with government mandated environmental costs. These rates charged to electric utility customers may be increased or decreased in an amount per kilowatt hour (kWh) through an environmental compliance cost recovery rider. In keeping with sound financial management practices, the policy of the city will be to ensure that its utilities are operated in a fiscally sound manner and as such to make environmental compliance cost recovery adjustment to pass on compliance costs for federal mandates to utility customers as needed.
(d) Environmental compliance cost recovery rider (ECCR): The monthly environmental compliance cost recovery adjustments in cents per kWh shall represent the difference between annually reported environmental compliance costs from MEAG divided by the total kilowatt hour sold to customers served under tariffs subject to such environmental compliance cost recovery rider. Application of this rider is at the sole discretion of the City of East Point. Applicable tariffs include residential, general service, small power, medium power, and large power.
(e) Economic mitigation: Economic mitigation shall mean a decrease (credit) in rates charged to the residential class of customers. (i) Senior residential discount electric utility customers, age sixty-five (65) or older on January 1st of any calendar year may receive a seven-dollar ($7.00) per month discount on electric service for no more than one (1) residential account. To be eligible, the senior citizen must continuously meet all of the following criteria:
1) The senior citizen must be the named residential account holder;
2) The senior citizen account holder must be a full-time resident at the location where utility services are provided;
